# STUDIO — ROUND 3 — THE FULL BOARD

Salvaged from three workflow journals after two container restarts killed the
run mid-flight. 8 team reviews, their skeptics where they got that far, and the
narrative reports from the agents that finished.

**UNVERIFIED.** These are leads, not facts. See `docs/GOVERNOR.md` for the
standing rules and the ledger — round 2's board was confidently backwards about
which world the hero grinned in, and round 3 has already caught ME in a false
PASS (the food-truck wheels). Check every claim against the source before acting.

Round 3 has already produced, verified and shipped:
  - the grade's toe deleting colour channels (confirmed by pixel census)
  - the food truck's wheels rendering as holes (confirmed, fixed, and it
    exposed a false PASS in qa/blackprops.mjs)

  [major] Game Day's vehicles have no tonal separation between a horizontal face and a vertical one — settles ledger OPEN finding #6, and the ledger's diagnosis is only half the cause
    evidence: I cropped and measured, not eyeballed. /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/store/06-gameday.png, one crimson pickup, box 32,355 275x200 (`node qa/_boxhist.mjs`): rgb(168,0,0) 22.6%, rgb(172,0,0) 10.9%, rgb(171,0,0) 1.0%, rgb(50,0,0) 4.2%. /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/qa/_facemap.mjs colour-codes those bands and shows the assignment unambiguously: 168 is the cab roof and bed floor (up-faces), 172 is the long flank (side), 50 is the far vertical faces. A scanline across the body (`node qa/_scanline.mjs store/06-gameday.png 60 500 175 385 40`) walks flank rgb(172,0,0) -> bed interior -> roof rgb(168,0,0). So cab-top:body-side = 0.0855:0.0902 linear luminance = **1.055:1, and INVERTED** — the side is brighter than the top. This is NOT a red-channel problem: the cream pickup in the same frame (box 830,850 330x250) is rgb(198,177,148) against rgb(200,177,142) = **1.002:1** with no channel anywhere near zero. Population level, play area only (`node qa/_redband.mjs`): 327,900 red-dominant pixels, 84.3% with G=B=0, and **54.6% inside a single 12/255 band (163-174)**, 79.9% inside 150-190 — across dozens of vehicles, canopies and tents at every heading in the lot. THE BAR, from this game's own work: the same class of prop in Maple — makeFoodtruckFB, a painted box vehicle — measures roof rgb(206,176,39) against flank rgb(124,94,0) = **3.70:1**, one hard step at the roof line (`node qa/_scanline.mjs store/03-devouring.png 300 1930 300 2050 30`). CAUSE, and this is where the ledger is incomplete: prototype3d.ts:698 gives Game Day `off: [-38, 72, 78]`, elevation 39.7 degrees with horizontal magnitude 0.771 against sin(el) 0.639 — a sun-facing vertical face receives 21% MORE key than a horizontal one, and the hemisphere hands the top just enough back to cancel it. Maple's `off: [-55, 95, 42]` is 55.5 degrees, 0.825 against 0.565, so its boxes fold. Channel-crush makes the crimson unable to carry hue as well, but the flat read is there in a cream truck with three live channels.
    why: Every truck in the lot — and docs/GAMEDAY.md makes the lot the hero district — is a flat red or flat cream silhouette with a black notch cut in it. A child cannot see that a truck has a roof, a bonnet and a flank; it is a sticker on the tarmac. It is also the one world where the vehicle is the thing you are eating, so the object the whole level is made of is the object with no form in it.
    fix: Do NOT touch the light rig — the per-world spread is ledger #5, an owner call. Fix it where MOVERS owns it: bake the fold into the vertex colours at build time, exactly as bakeContactAO (island.ts:3807) already bakes the base shade. Add `sideShade(geo, k)` beside it in /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/src/proto3d/island.ts — walk the `normal` attribute and multiply the `color` attribute by k where |n.y| < 0.5 — and call it on the vehicle parts in /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/src/proto3d/tailgate.ts:287-303 (makeTailgateTruck's body/cab/bonnet/bed panels) only, so no other world moves. COLOUR SPACE, stated because retraction 3 exists: island.ts:3739 is `_pc.setHex(col)` and the comment at :3740 confirms three's ColorManagement makes those LINEAR, stored Uint16-normalised — so multiplying the colour attribute is a LINEAR multiply and the displayed step is k^(1/2.2). Use k = 0.52 linear = 0.745 displayed, which is exactly the CRIM (0xc4342f) -> CRIM_D (0x922520) relationship tailgate.ts:27-28 already authors and calls 'shadowed crimson, undersides and trim'. Zero triangles, zero draw calls, build time only — it also survives any future change to the sun angle, which a lighting fix would not.
    seeded draws: ZERO. sideShade is a pass over two attribute buffers on already-built geometry. No pick(), no Math.random, no mulberry draw added, removed or reordered; Maple is not touched at all.
    measure: Two gates. (1) Per-vehicle fold: for each vehicle mesh, brightest horizontal face against brightest sun-facing vertical face in LINEAR luminance, bar >= 1.8:1. Reason for 1.8: the game's own authored shadow-crimson step is 1.92:1, and Maple's food truck already renders 3.70:1, so 1.8 is below what this game demonstrably reaches on the same prop. Today Game Day crimson 1.055:1, cream 1.002:1 — FAIL. (2) Population: share of red-dominant play-area pixels falling inside any single 12/255 band, bar < 25%; today 54.6% (qa/_redband.mjs). What else would move these numbers? A truck whose flank happens to face away from the sun would legitimately be darker — which is why gate (1) takes the BRIGHTEST vertical face, and why gate (2) is measured across the whole lot at every heading rather than off one truck.

  [major] The Maple food truck's wheels render as pure rgb(0,0,0) holes, and the hole probe misses them by its own MIN_AREA
    evidence: /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/store/03-devouring.png, box 20,1830 420x320: two connected pure-black blobs, 1785 px (62x42) and 1698 px (61x42), at solidity 0.995 and 0.992 (`node qa/_blackblob.mjs`, `node qa/_blacksolid.mjs`). Cropped at 4x they are hard-edged ellipses exactly at the wheel positions with no rim, no hub and no shading — they read as two holes punched under the truck, not as tyres. SOURCE: island.ts:4763 `new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 10), std(0x20242c, 0.9))` — one dark cylinder, nothing else. Same at island.ts:4707 (golfcart) and :4751 (icecream cart), ~16 placements across Maple and Pirate (island.ts:5879, 5927, 6189, 6190, 6573). Next door in the same repo, tailgate.ts's `wheelParts` pushes a CHAR tyre AND an `ALU` (0xc8ccd2) hub, and life.ts:437 makeCar pushes CAR_TYRE plus CAR_HUB (0xc9cdd6) — and those wheels read: the hub ellipses are plainly visible in store/06-gameday.png cropped at 930,1930 360x280 @4x. THE GATE MISSES IT AND SAYS PASS: `node qa/blackprops.mjs` reports '03-devouring.png 0 crushed prop face(s)'. Its solidity bar is 0.95 and these blobs are 0.99; the only thing keeping them out is `MIN_AREA = 2000` at qa/blackprops.mjs:104, and they are 1785 and 1698.
    why: At deviceScaleFactor 3 that is a 21x14 CSS-pixel hole — bigger than a HUD icon — sitting under a bright yellow truck on Maple's pale plaza, in a shipped App Store screenshot. A six-year-old is looking at a toy truck balanced on two black gaps. It is also the game contradicting itself: two other wheel builders in the same codebase get this right.
    fix: Give these three the hub the rest of the game already has. Smallest version: in /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/src/proto3d/island.ts:4707, :4751 and :4763, add a second cylinder at 0.5x the tyre radius and 1.1x the width in `std(0xc8ccd2, 0.4)` beside each tyre, matching tailgate.ts's wheelParts character for character. That is +4 meshes per vehicle on ~16 vehicles (+64 draw calls, +8 in Maple). Better and cheaper: rebuild all three fallbacks with part()/mergedProp() as tailgate.ts does — the foodtruck is currently 8 separate Meshes, so merging takes it to 1 and the hub becomes free. Net draw calls go DOWN.
    seeded draws: ZERO. These are fixed-position wheels inside a builder with no random call in the wheel loop; adding a mesh or changing a hex draws nothing. The placement sites (island.ts:5879, 5927) keep their existing rand() calls unchanged, and none of them are on Maple's mulberry stream.
    measure: Lower `MIN_AREA` in /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/qa/blackprops.mjs:104 from 2000 to 1200 and change nothing else — the probe then fails on 03-devouring.png today, because both blobs clear the existing 0.95 solidity bar at 0.995/0.992. 1200 device px at 3x is a 12x12 CSS-px object, which is still comfortably visible on a phone; the probe's own header already argues 2000 ~ 'visible', so this is tightening a threshold that was set generously, not inventing one. What else would move it? A genuinely convex cast shadow could newly qualify at the smaller area — so re-derive the solidity spread on the shipped set at the new MIN_AREA before committing the bar, exactly as the probe's header instructs.

  [major] qa/crowdface.mjs — the probe written to stop exactly this class of defect — has never photographed a head, and prints success
    evidence: I ran it: `node qa/crowdface.mjs 4177 maple` printed 'maple: 5 cloned crowd people, 5 head crops h3.59/px35 ...'. I then opened all five files in /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/qa/out/crowdface/. maple_head_0.png is a bush, a blue placard and a shoulder — no head. maple_head_3.png is a sun-hat brim and a shoulder — no head. maple_head_2.png is a gold torso and a clipboard with a head cut off at the top edge. maple_head_4.png is two bodies with both heads cut off above the frame. maple_head_1.png has a head, off-centre against the crop edge with a second person's hat in it. Zero of five crops are centred on a head. CAUSE, read in source: qa/crowdface.mjs:62-67 computes the crop centre from `bb = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(c)` and projects `bb.max.y + 0.1` and `bb.max.y - 1.2`. `setFromObject` on a whole person includes hand props — a placard is `pc(B.tube, ..., 2.30*s)` plus a panel held above the head (life.ts:757-760) — so bb.max.y is the top of the PLACARD, and the crop lands 1.3 units below that, on the chest. It also still has no self-assertion, which is the exact hardening the round-2 skeptic asked for ('assert per-crop channel variance above a floor') and which was never added. This is the direct reason finding #1 above is in two shipped App Store screenshots: the crown is the one part of a walking person no instrument in this repo has ever looked at. qa/personsheet.mjs cannot see movers at all (retraction 9, radius filter 0.5-1.6 against 2.4/1.9); its successor can select them and then photographs their torsos.
    why: Not directly a child-facing defect — it is the reason child-facing defects ship. Retraction 1 (white eyeballs), retraction 9 (the sheet that never photographed a walker) and finding #1 above are the same failure three times: the crowd's head is the surface the play camera spends most of its time on and the surface no probe has ever resolved. A probe that reports '5 head crops' while writing five pictures of shoulders is worse than no probe, because it closes the question.
    fix: /home/user/voidling/artifacts/3d-game/qa/crowdface.mjs:62 — centre the crop on the head's own node, not the whole-object bbox. makePerson attaches it: `g.userData.limbs = { ..., head: hd }` at src/proto3d/life.ts:1162, and it is read the same way at life.ts:2670, so capture `q.m.userData.limbs.head` and its world Y BEFORE the clone (the probe blanks userData on the clone at :57) and project `c.position.y + headYOffset` plus/minus the head's own half-height. Then add the self-assertion the round-2 skeptic specified: after each crop, fail if per-channel pixel variance is below a floor, and fail if the crop contains no skin/hair-range pixels. Both are probe-only, zero runtime cost.
    seeded draws: ZERO — test code only, and it operates on clones that are not in `movers` and not registered as edibles.
    measure: The probe asserts on itself: five crops written, each with per-channel variance above a floor and a non-zero share of head-coloured pixels inside the middle third. Today 0 of 5 pass. Pair it with the head-cover bar from finding #1 so the numeric gate and the photograph are checking the same subject — the lesson of retraction 8 is that a probe passing and a frame failing are not in conflict when they measure different things.

WHAT IS GOOD:
Protect these — I cropped each one and they are at the bar.

**`roofKit`, `mainstreet.ts:222-243`.** The only place in the game that has internalised "the camera looks down, so the roof is the facade": AC plant scaled to `w*d/34`, vent stacks at 0.8x that, a skylight over 8x7, a 45%-chance access hatch. Crucially its palette is separated properly — ROOF_TAR 0x4e5560 / ROOF_DUCT 0xaeb6c2 / ROOF_VENT 0x8b93a0 at `:163` is a 2.3:1 value step, so the furniture reads when it is in frame. Every other world should be copying this. (Caveat for the shooter, not for STATIC: in `store/03-devouring.png` only a sliver of one roof is in frame at 0,115 and it shows none of the furniture — a 60x30 patch measures 95.9% one value. The kit is right; the framing is not showing it.)

**The bathhouse eave lines, `nightmarket.ts:455-472`.** Drawing a building's shape in unlit glow because the play camera cannot see its vertical faces is the best static idea in the repo. Measured in `store/05`: a flat `rgb(243,162,57)`, L 171.7, 100% of a 120x8 sample. They are the only reason the finale is legible from anywhere in the valley. My finding 3 is about the fill under them, not the lines — keep every one.

**`makeStall`'s lit back wall and griddle, `nightmarket.ts:227-230`.** A `G_AMBER` panel *behind* the counter so the stallholder is silhouetted against it, plus a `G_GRIDDLE` slot on the counter. A lighting idea baked into a prop at zero light cost. In every stall crop I took (04 at 980,280 and 150,350, 4-5x) that orange slot is the only thing making the row read as inhabited. It is currently carrying the entire market.

**`makeMarketShed`'s pitched canopy, `nightmarket.ts:1052-1055`.** Two slopes rotated ±0.5 rad with a `VERM_D` ridge cap along the crest. This is the kit finding 1 asks `makeStall` to adopt — it already exists, eleven lines away, in the same file, at the same cost.

**`makeCanopy`'s pitch, `tailgate.ts:322`.** `ConeGeometry(2.6, 0.95, 4)` is a real 27° pitch and it works: the four facets measurably separate in `store/06` at rgb(174,0,0) / rgb(163,0,0) / rgb(129,0,0), a 1.35:1 break. Do not flatten this while fixing finding 7.

**`makeLawnSign` + `signLines`, `mainstreet.ts:772-810`.** The RATIO table ("no two adjacent rows the same length: equal bars read as a barcode") plus the rosette. Cropped at 4x in two separate places in `store/03` (180,1620 and 200,240) it reads as a fair sign at 40 device pixels, and `FAIR_SIGN`'s three colours are genuinely reachable through `SIDE()` at `island.ts:6139`. This holds up under magnification.

**`makeFlowers` post-fix, `island.ts:4437`.** The squashed sphere with seated, stemmed blossoms reads as a planting from directly above, with no facets and nothing hanging in the air. Cropped at 6x in two places. The most-placed small prop in Maple is now correct — leave it alone.

**The Maple storefront kit's street level, `mainstreet.ts:574-579`.** Awning, stall riser, sill bars and sign band. At 2.5x (`store/03` 0,140) the shopfront reads as an actual shop. The upstairs is what fails, not the shopfront.

  [blocker] Lantern Night's stall canopy is a flat monochrome slab, and it is a quarter of the world's headline frame
    evidence: SOURCE: `src/proto3d/nightmarket.ts:214-215` — two axis-aligned `BoxGeometry` at y=`h` and y=`h-0.1` with no rotation arguments at all, under the comment at `:213` that reads "the canopy: a shallow ridge". Rise is literally 0. `island.ts:5088` requests 230 of them under the comment "This is the level", and `nightmarket.ts:88-97` records the vermilion canopy as "45% of the world's triangles".
PIXELS, `store/04-lantern-market.png`: crops at 0,740 620x400 (3x) and 0,1860 720x700 (1.4x) — three or four adjacent canopies run into one unbroken red bar with no ridge, no seam and no eave shadow anywhere along it. Masking the canopy-red family across the play area (y 150..2586): **790,190 px = 25.15% of the frame**, and **61.4% of that mask sits within ±2 display levels of just two values, L=16 and L=26**. Largest single 4-connected region of that family: **174,911 px, bounding box 703x679** — 55% of the screen width in one shape. The top plate measures rgb(97,5,12), L 25.1; the market floor 60 px away measures rgb(37,26,26), L 28.4 — the biggest surface in the world is also darker than the ground it stands on.
THE BAR IS THE PROJECT'S OWN APPROVED ART: `store/02-worlds.png` crop 660,1300 440x300 (3x). The Lantern Night poster's awnings are pitched, ridged and striped red-and-cream. I am not proposing any change to the poster.
    why: A six-year-old scanning for the next thing to eat sees one continuous red plane over a quarter of the screen. She cannot tell where one stall ends and the next begins, cannot tell a stall from a table, and cannot count how many there are. The stripe that would fix it is already built — `nightmarket.ts:216-222` hangs six alternating PAPER/VERM_D bands off the FRONT valance. At this camera (`prototype3d.ts:575`, camOffset (0.62,0.92,0.62) → 46.4° elevation) the canopy top projects ~9.7 square units and that valance ~1.8: the prop's only pattern sits on the face worth one fifth of the face the camera reads, and on every stall I cropped it is hidden behind the canopy overhang.
    fix: `nightmarket.ts:214-215` → `makeMarketShed`'s kit, with the eave pinned at today's height so nothing below it moves:
`for (const sz of [-1,1]) solid.push(part(new THREE.BoxGeometry(wD*1.17, 0.16, dD*0.66), VERM, 0, h + dD*0.135, sz*dD*0.30, sz*-0.42, 0, 0));`
`solid.push(part(new THREE.BoxGeometry(wD*1.19, 0.20, 0.30), VERM_D, 0, h + dD*0.27, 0));`
Half-slope depth dD*0.33 × sin(0.42) = dD*0.135, so the outer eave lands at exactly y=h and the valance at `:216-222` needs no move. +1 part, +12 triangles per stall, ~2.8k for all 230. 0 draw calls and 0 materials — both go into the same `mergedProp(solid)` inside `lit()` at `nightmarket.ts:114-119` — and Lantern is not the memory-bound world.
    seeded draws: Zero. `nightmarket.ts:111` defines `rnd` as `Math.random`; `island.ts:5032 plant()` and `:5088 stallSlots(Math.random, …)` scatter on `Math.random` too. Lantern never touches the mulberry32 stream, so Maple's placement at `mainstreet.ts:252` is byte-identical.

========================================================================
TEAM REVIEW — VERDICT NO-SHIP
========================================================================
WHAT IS GOOD:
Four things on this surface are better than the genre and must not be touched.

1. THE MENU (store/01-menu.png). Best-in-class. The logo lockup sits in the sky, the key art's island and the void's face are completely clear of every glyph, and PLAY is one enormous unambiguous red target with nothing competing. The four nav tiles are equal-width, full-colour emoji over 16.8:1 white labels — a child who cannot read still navigates by icon. Measured: all four card boxes identical at 223 device px, SCRAPBOOK's "0/60" at 9.76:1. Do not add anything to this screen.

2. THE GROWTH BAR (visible in 03, 04, 05, 06). The single best-designed HUD element in the build: a near-opaque plate, form name in white at 13px with a shadow, metres in gold, "NEXT COLOSSUS" in lavender at the right, and tick marks on the track at the next two thresholds so a six-year-old can see how far it is. It answers "how big am I / what am I next / how close" in one glance and it never moves. It is also the element finding #1 is defending — fix the bubble, do not touch the bar.

3. THE WORLD-PICKER TYPE TREATMENT, and the reserved lines behind it. `#worlds .wCard b/span/.wBest` (index.html:958-962) wear a 2.5px stroke painted UNDER the fill with `paint-order: stroke fill`, plus two tight glows — and it works: MAPLE FALLS reads cleanly straight over a lit island with no scrim at all, on approved poster art nobody had to repaint. That is the right idiom and it is exactly what `#count` and `.vf` are missing. The min-height reservations at :984 and :999 also genuinely hold — I measured title-to-PLAY at exactly 275 device px on four of five cards INCLUDING Game Day, whose subtitle wraps to two lines. The fix from 62a4a31 works. Do not undo it to "save space".

4. THE RESULTS SCREEN'S STRUCTURE (store/08-results.png). The ranked rows with the player's own row highlighted in gold at 9.72:1, the count-up ceremony with eight rising pops, the "STILL HIDING · THE BEACH" hook at 12.70:1, the stat tiles, the gold-outlined NEW BEST, and the sticky PLAY AGAIN row with its 28px gradient apron and reserved bottom padding (index.html:709-722) — all of it is correct and all of it was argued in writing. The screen's problem is one line of copy, not its architecture.

Also worth protecting because a later round will want to "fix" it: `#timer` is deliberately NOT centred. `left: 42vw; right: 8px` (index.html:120) puts it at +84 CSS px right of screen centre — I measured +84 in the frame, matching the CSS exactly — because the board owns the left. It is authored, it is commented, and it is right. And the safe-area discipline is real: 19 `env(safe-area-inset-*)` uses, `.endGo` reserves the home-indicator inset, and `.backBtn` measures exactly 44.0 CSS px tall in the shipped frame.

    fix: Two declarations, the idiom already used three times in this repo (index.html:126 on #timer, index.html:958-962 on the picker titles): `.vf { -webkit-text-stroke: 3px rgba(12,6,26,0.92); paint-order: stroke fill; }` and `.vf.big { -webkit-text-stroke: 4px rgba(12,6,26,0.92); }` at bubbles.ts:145/148. Measured on that stroke: pink 7.75:1, mint 13.37:1, independent of world. Keep both colours — they are the identity; the stroke just stops them carrying the contrast job alone. While in the file, `font-weight: 900 → 700` at :144 and :137 and `800 → 700` at :110: prototype3d.ts:24-27 imports only 400/500/600/700 and index.html:71 sets font-synthesis:none, so those three declarations render 700 and lie about it.
    seeded draws: Zero. text-stroke and paint-order do not affect the box, so slot.w/slot.h measured at bubbles.ts:269-270 and the de-collision maths are untouched.
    measure: qa/contrast2.mjs:33 is the right instrument (shoot with the overlay hidden, shoot with it shown, take the changed pixels as the chrome, measure the chrome's own internal range — scene-independent by construction). Its ID list is `['board','timer','coins','btnQuit','growth']`. Expose `__float(text)` on the debug object, fire one over the Maple plaza with the void parked, take the changed pixels; assert internal step ≥ 7:1. Fails today at ~1.2:1. And add contrast2 to the `push` profile in qa/gate.mjs — it is in no profile at all.

  [major] Five system-font glyphs sit inside Fredoka words, four of them on primary controls — including one round 2's codepoint audit missed
    evidence: Measured in the shipped frames. store/08-results.png cropped at 4x: the `→` on OPEN SHOP has a shaft 4 device px thick against Fredoka 700 letter stems of 7 device px in the same word (57%), with a flat mechanical arrowhead beside fully-rounded terminals. store/03-devouring.png cropped at 7x: the `⌂` home button renders as a hollow pentagon 30 device px wide (10 CSS px) with 5-device-px (1.67 CSS px) walls inside a 44 CSS px button set at font-size: 20px (index.html:1026) — 23% of the button's width, and the only line-art icon in a UI where every other icon is a full-colour emoji (📗 🛍️ 🏆 👑 ⚙️ ✨ 💎 🔥). store/02-worlds.png: the `▶` on all five PLAY chips is a sharp geometric triangle. I re-resolved every codepoint in src/ and index.html against the real unicode-range lists in node_modules/@fontsource/fredoka/700.css: the latin subset covers U+2191 and U+2193 but NOT U+2192, so `→` at prototype3d.ts:4810 ("TAKE ME THERE →") and :4843 ("OPEN SHOP →") is a FIFTH uncovered glyph that round 2's audit did not list. The other four are ✦ U+2726 (the currency mark, on screen every frame and in every coin floater), ⌂ U+2302 (index.html:1764, prototype3d.ts:6347/6410), ✕ U+2715, ▶ U+25B6 (index.html:1868 plus all five world cards at :1904/:1909/:1914/:1919/:1924).
    why: These are the buttons a pre-reader navigates by shape. "Go home" is a 1.67px hollow pentagon; "buy things" is a hairline arrow half the weight of the word next to it; "play this world" is a triangle from a different type family. A child who cannot read the word reads the mark, and the mark is a placeholder.
    fix: Replace all five with owned shapes, ~400 bytes of one inline `<svg><defs>` block referenced with `<use>`: `✦` → one four-point star defined once (it is the currency mark; it should be an asset, not a fallback); `▶` → a CSS triangle on a ::before (`border-left: 9px solid currentColor`); `→` → an SVG arrow whose shaft matches Fredoka's 700 stem ratio; `✕` → two rotated 2px spans; `⌂` → an SVG house with a roof overhang and a door at Fredoka's stroke weight. This also removes a real iOS risk: none of the five is guaranteed text presentation on every iOS version, and `▶` flips to emoji presentation on some.
    seeded draws: Zero.
    measure: qa/glyphs.mjs — static, no browser, sub-second. Parse the unicode-range lists out of the four @fontsource/fredoka/*.css files, scan index.html markup outside `<style>` plus every string assigned to innerHTML/textContent in src/, fail on any codepoint ≥ U+0100 that is neither covered nor emoji-presentation (carries U+FE0F or lives in the pictograph blocks). Fails today with exactly 5 DOM-bound hits; passes after. Goes straight into the `push` profile.

  [major] Nothing in the bubble system knows where the hero is — and the probe built to prove it is wired to no gate
    evidence: CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF FIRST, measured: in store/03-devouring.png the lower bubble is NOT across his chin. Measured bounding boxes — hero disc bottom y=1585 device, bubble plate top y=1526, mouth centre ≈ y=1365. The bubble covers the bottom 59 device px (19.7 CSS px, 11% of the disc height) and clears the mouth by 161 device px (54 CSS px). That is a body clip, which qa/bubbleclear.mjs's own header calls "fine and unavoidable". The upper bubble is clear of him entirely. So shot 03 is a near miss, not a hit — and it must not be reported as one. What IS true is structural, read in source: dodge() runs only over hudR (bubbles.ts:329-333, from HUD_AVOID) and bandR (:335-342, from HUD_BANDS), both of which are lists of DOM ids resolved with getElementById. The void is a 3D object with no DOM node, so nothing in update() can know where he is. The one thing on screen that must never be covered is the only thing with no rule protecting it, and the crowd nearest him is exactly the crowd most likely to be talking (life.ts feeds bubbles.say from proximity, prototype3d.ts:1869).
    why: The hero sits dead centre of the frame for 180 seconds. A bubble that lands 60px higher than the one in shot 03 sits on his eyes. Nobody knows how often that happens, because it has never been measured on a build.
    fix: Give the dodge loop one rect that is not a DOM id. bubbles.update(dt) is called at prototype3d.ts:8802 where voidling.group.position and R are both in scope — pass them (`bubbles.update(dt, voidling.group.position, R)`), project with the camera bubbles.ts already holds, and push the FACE rect (upper-middle of the disc, ~62% of its width, exactly as qa/bubbleclear.mjs's header defines it) into hudR before the existing loop at bubbles.ts:396. The rest is free: dodge() prefers ABOVE, which for a centre-screen hero is correct.
    seeded draws: Zero. Projection and DOM layout only.
    measure: qa/bubbleclear.mjs already exists (committed f89795a), already drives the autopilot, already computes the face rect, and already carries a stated bar with a stated reason (MAX_FACE_COVER = 0.03 — not zero, because a bubble mid-fade as the hero moves under it is legitimate). `grep -rn bubbleclear` finds it referenced by nothing but itself: not qa/gate.mjs, not package.json, not a doc. RUN IT, record the real number in the ledger, then add it to the `push` profile. A probe written for a defect and never connected is how this one shipped.

  [major] The trophy moment reads "🏆 REGULAR EARNED!" and throws away the trophy's own icon
    evidence: store/08-results.png, headline crop at 2x: the lead line under the result reads "🏆 REGULAR EARNED!". Source: prototype3d.ts:4735 (and the solo path at :4655) builds it as `` `🏆 ${troPay.last.toUpperCase()} EARNED!` ``, where `last` is a trophy's `nm` from the TROPHIES table. Reading that table (prototype3d.ts:6470-6483), three of the twelve names break the template: 'Regular' (:6483) → "REGULAR EARNED!", 'Bottomless' (:6477) → "BOTTOMLESS EARNED!", 'Bigger Than Auntie' (:6478) → "BIGGER THAN AUNTIE EARNED!". Every trophy also carries its own `ic` — 📅 for Regular, 🌌 for Bottomless, ⚡ for Bigger Than Auntie — and payTrophies() (:6490-6503) returns only `last: string`, so the icon is discarded and a generic cup is substituted.
    why: This is the reward beat — the loudest positive line on a screen that otherwise leads with "#6". A six-year-old reads "REGULAR EARNED" and learns nothing: not what they got, not what it looks like, not that there is a shelf of them. The trophy has a picture and the screen shows a different picture. And this is what went out in the App Store screenshot.
    fix: Two small changes. (1) payTrophies() at prototype3d.ts:6503 already has the trophy object in hand — return `ic` alongside `last`: `return { …, last: due[due.length-1].nm, icon: due[due.length-1].ic }`. (2) Change the template at :4735 and :4655 to a form that is grammatical for all twelve names and shows the real mark: `` `${troPay.icon} NEW TROPHY · ${troPay.last.toUpperCase()}` ``. No name needs rewriting, no copy review, and it stays correct for the thirteenth trophy.
    seeded draws: Zero.
    measure: Static, no browser — qa/trophycopy.mjs: import TROPHIES, render the lead template for all twelve, assert every result matches `^<one emoji> NEW TROPHY · [A-Z0-9 '·-]+$`, that the emoji equals that trophy's own `ic`, and that no rendered lead exceeds the width #end .sub can hold at clamp(16px,4.6vw,20px) on a 375px phone. Fails today on the template shape for all twelve (generic 🏆) and on grammar for three; passes after. Runs in milliseconds, goes in `push`.

  [minor] Shop card names have no reserved second line, so the price row breaks alignment by 19 CSS px — the exact fault the world picker already documented and fixed
    evidence: store/07-skins.png, measured: the gold "$2.99" on the Shadow Ninja card starts at y=2213 while the "$2.99" on Drako beside it starts at y=2156 — a 57 device px / 19.0 CSS px step between two cards in the same row. Cropped at 3x and confirmed by eye: "Shadow" / "Ninja" wraps to two lines and shoves the price down. Source: `.skCard .nm` (index.html:1573) sets font-size and weight and no min-height; `.skCard .pr` (:1574) follows it in normal flow. The picker next door hit this identically, wrote 12 lines about it, and fixed it — index.html:984 `min-height: 2.5em` on the subtitle and :999 `min-height: 2.4em` on .wBest, with the comment "TWO LINES ARE ALWAYS RESERVED, even though every subtitle currently fits on one… so a translation cannot either." That reasoning was never carried across the file. 'Shadow Ninja' is the only 12-character name today; the next one, or any localisation, breaks another row.
    why: Five cards in a grid with one price sitting lower than its neighbour reads as a broken screen, and this is the screen where a child is being asked for $2.99. The shop is the one surface that has to look expensive.
    fix: One declaration at index.html:1573: `.skCard .nm { … min-height: 2.4em; }` (2 lines at 15px with the inherited line-height). The grid rows already stretch, so nothing else moves and the price line lands at the same y on every card whatever the name says.

Add: `const ys = [...document.querySelectorAll('#shopGrid .skCard .pr')].map(e => Math.round(e.getBoundingClientRect().top))`, group by grid row, assert every row's spread is 0. Fails today on the legendary row (19px); passes after. Do the same assertion for `.skCard .nm` tops so the next long name cannot reintroduce it.

  [minor] On the menu, the SCRAPBOOK tile's icon and label sit 7 CSS px higher than the other three
    evidence: store/01-menu.png, measured: all four .navCard boxes are identical (y 2462–2684, h 223 device px — the grid stretch works), but the pure-white label cap-top is y=2580 on SCRAPBOOK against y=2601 on SHOP, TROPHIES and TOP VOIDS — a 21 device px / 7.0 CSS px spread. Visible in a 5x crop of the row. Cause: only #btnBook carries a second line (`<em id="bookCount">` at index.html:1809, filled with "0/60" by prototype3d.ts:5990), and `.navCard` (index.html:1285) is a `<button>` with no display or alignment set, so the UA centres its content block vertically inside the stretched box — taller content pushes the icon and label UP.

  [minor] The shop's parental-purchase line is the lowest-contrast text on the screen, at 4.11:1 against the project's own 4.5:1 floor
    evidence: store/07-skins.png, footer cropped at 2x and sampled: ink rgb(126,104,166) on ground rgb(13,8,34) = 4.11:1. Source: `#shopLegal { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: rgba(201,166,255,0.6) }` at index.html:1528, carrying "purchases are made through the App Store. ask a grown-up before you buy." (markup :2034). The 0.6 alpha is doing all of it. ========================================================================
TEAM REVIEW — VERDICT NO-SHIP
========================================================================
WHAT IS GOOD:
"Four things on this character are genuinely world-class and must not be touched while the above is fixed.\n\n1. THE RESTING GRIN. The two-tone mouth — dark rim 0x2a0e2e over a lighter inner 0xff6f91, both skin-blind so the pair carries its own contrast — is the best-authored feature in the game. Cropped at 8x from four different worlds (scratchpad/m03, m04, m06, and the clean live render scratchpad/maw3/grin-maw0p0001.png) it reads as an opening with depth on a near-black body and on a near-white one alike, and the half-disc-inside-a-half-disc nesting makes the containment structural rather than arithmetic. The reasoning recorded at void3d.ts:975-1040 — that a LIGHT rim over a DARK middle is lipstick and a DARK rim over a LIGHTER middle is a cavity — is correct and is why the white plate had to go. Do not reshape the lip or the inner, and do not re-route either colour against the skin.\n\n2. THE EYES' BAKED TEXTURES. 512px sclera and pupil with the lid shadow, the warm underside bounce, the iris falloff, the violet reflected crescent and both catchlights painted in (void3d.ts:786-860). Cropped at 8x (scratchpad/eye06.png) it holds up at 130 device px and still reads at 40. It retired four meshes doing it. This is the asset the whole character rests on.\n\n3. THE PIT MOVED OFF THE FACE. Dropping the abyss core into the belly at N.xy = (0,-0.46) instead of the disc centre (void3d.ts:252-261) is the single decision that makes the face legible — face on top, open space below it. Every crop in this pass shows the eyes sitting on a dark ground that never swallows them.\n\n4. THE RIM MEASURED IN PIXELS. `rimStop = clamp(1.0 - 2.5/max(8.0,uPxR), 0.90, 0.985)` (void3d.ts:~232) is what killed both \"our voids purple faded\" and \"there's a ring around him\". A rim expressed as a fraction of the disc RADIUS eats the disc's AREA quadratically; expressing it as a pixel width does not. Never re-express this as a disc fraction, and never re-add uRim on top of the rim mix.\n\nAlso right, and cheap to lose by accident: no teeth anywhere (the owner's call, and mkFang correctly builds and never adds); the blush fading out as he shrinks so the two brightest parts of the silhouette do not grey down; and FACE_WRAP at 0.62, which seats the features on the form without turning the outer eye into a hard ellipse."

  [blocker] The bite gape is PORTRAIT and NARROWER than the closed grin — the mouth shrinks when it opens, so it reads as a gasp, not a chomp
    evidence: Rendered, not argued. I drove the live rig (maple, r=7, real match camera) and shot the gape at maw 0.25/0.4/0.55/0.7/0.85/1.0/1.1 — /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-voidling/2a240c97-4d5b-5823-ac36-95bed2f17b29/scratchpad/maw3/ship-1.png and ship-0.55.png. Both read as an "oh!": a tall dark egg with a small pink lozenge parked in the bottom fifth. Exact geometry, by projecting the meshes' own bounding boxes through the match camera (qa/_scratch/mawgeom.mjs, so no colour threshold can be fooled by the eyes): resting grin aspect 3.55:1 LANDSCAPE (void3d.ts:1039, lip 0.178r x scale(1.34,0.76) = 0.477w x 0.135h); gape aspect 0.88:1 PORTRAIT at EVERY maw value (void3d.ts:1054, mawDark 0.2r x scale(1,1.15) = 0.400w x 0.460h). That is a 4.0x aspect flip between the two mouths of one character, and the shape is scale-invariant so the gasp read is not a transient. Worse, the gape at FULL open is 0.400 wide against the resting grin's 0.477 (cruise) / 0.525 (hungry, mp.smile 1.1) / 0.677 (frenzy, 1.42) — 16%, 24% and 41% NARROWER. void3d.ts:1000 states the design intent outright: "the little smile and the big gape are now the same mouth at two sizes instead of two unrelated designs." The shipped scales do the opposite. Ledger #3b's measured duty cycle (qa/faceparity.mjs raw grin share: Maple 28%) means this is the face for ~72% of a Maple match.
    why: Eating is the only verb in this game. A six-year-old's reward for swallowing a house is the hero's face, and for three frames out of four that face is 😮 — a small, tall, dark hole that says "oh no" — instead of a chomp. The mouth getting SMALLER as it opens is the specific thing that kills it: a child reads "open wide" as wider, and the rig delivers 16-41% narrower.
    fix: Two literals, void3d.ts:1054-1055. `mawDark.scale.set(1, 1.15, 1)` -> `mawDark.scale.set(1.25, 1.0, 1)`; `tongue.scale.set(1.15, 0.7, 1)` -> `tongue.scale.set(1.45, 0.78, 1)` and `tongue.position.set(0, -0.09, 0.01)` -> `(0, -0.06, 0.01)`. Measured result (same projection probe): gape aspect 0.88 -> 1.26, gape width 0.400 -> 0.500 (now WIDER than the cruise grin's 0.477 instead of 16% narrower), tongue area share of the gape 0.252 -> 0.326, tongue centre lifts from 0.198 to 0.153 of the gape height below centre. Rendered A/B: scratchpad/maw3/d-l125-1.png and d-l125-0.55.png against ship-1.png / ship-0.55.png — it reads as an open mouth at both. The round-2 board's own proposal (1.34, 0.92 / 1.50, 0.70 — c-l134-1.png) also clears the bar (aspect 1.47) and is a legitimate alternative; I prefer 1.25x1.00 because 0.92 height makes the gape shorter than the grin is deep and the tongue starts to read as a lip. I am NOT touching chomp()'s retrigger rule (owner-only) and NOT touching MOUTH_HIDES_AT.
    seeded draws: Zero. void3d.ts contains no mrnd/mr/mpick/mchance call at all (grep count 0), so Maple's placement stream is byte-identical.
    measure: New qa/gapeshape.mjs, modelled on qa/_scratch/mawgeom.mjs: enter a match, find the maw and mouth groups in the live scene, project each mesh's geometry bounding box through the match camera, and assert (a) gapeW/gapeH >= 1.00 and (b) gapeW at maw=1 >= lipW at mp.smile=1. Bars are definitional, not taste: a mouth opening taller than it is wide is the universal drawing of a gasp, and a mouth that narrows as it opens contradicts the word "open". Today it reads 0.88 and 0.400-vs-0.477 and fails both.

  [blocker] The eye outline is written through Color.setRGB in LINEAR space, so the "dark boundary" renders at 1.00:1 contrast against the body — and as a lavender ring on every non-purple skin
    evidence: void3d.ts:869-870 authors the outline `0x2a1f45` and the comment at :2094 states its job: "the eye keeps a dark boundary against a bright body". void3d.ts:1905-1906 then rewrites it every frame as `color.setRGB(0x2a/255*k, 0x1f/255*k, 0x45/255*k)`. In three r185 (node_modules/three/package.json 0.185.1) `Color.setRGB(r,g,b, colorSpace = ColorManagement.workingColorSpace)` (Color.js:227) defaults to LinearSRGB, so sRGB-normalised components go in undecoded — retraction #3's exact failure mode, in the file this team owns. Read back off the LIVE material (qa/_scratch/eyeoutline.mjs, maple, r=7): displayed rgb(124,107,155) where the author's 0x2a1f45 at the same k=1.216 would display rgb(47,35,76). Confirmed in rendered pixels, not just in the material: scratchpad/snout/classic.png at y=270 crosses the left eye's edge as body rgb(140,89,211) -> outline rgb(122,109,155) -> sclera rgb(191,186,200). WCAG contrast of that outline against the body immediately beside it is 1.00:1 — it is exactly as bright as the thing it is supposed to separate the eye from, and only reads at all because it is desaturated. The store set shows the same value: store/06-gameday.png at (380,1117) is rgb(113,98,149) against body rgb(132,77,208) = 1.02:1. On non-purple skins it is worse than invisible, it is the WRONG HUE: scratchpad/snout/rexling.png and drako.png put a mid-lavender gasket around a green and a teal eye.
    why: The eyes are the character — this repo already burned a retraction on eyeballs. At 1.00:1 the eye has no edge where the body is light (his whole upper-left cheek), so it reads as pasted on rather than set in; and on the two $2.99 dinosaur skins a child sees a purple plastic rim glued around each eyeball.
    fix: One line, void3d.ts:1905-1906. Replace the three-component setRGB with `color.setHex(0x2a1f45).multiplyScalar(k)` — setHex decodes sRGB->linear, then multiplyScalar scales in linear, which is what "lit by k" physically means and matches shade()/tint() in island.ts. Note the sibling line :1904, `e.white.material.color.setScalar(k)`, is CORRECT and must not be changed: a white sclera texture wants a linear light multiplier, and the measured sclera (204-217) is what k=0.62..1.22 should give.
    seeded draws: Zero.
    measure: Extend qa/voidsheet.mjs, which already enforces >=3:1 for the mouth against the body (the bar this house set at void3d.ts:975-990 after six of eight skins failed it). Add: for each skin, sample the 2px band immediately outside the sclera and the body annulus immediately outside that, and require WCAG >= 3:1. Same bar, same reason — a feature whose only job is to read against the body needs 3:1. Today it measures 1.00:1 on the DEFAULT skin in a live play frame.

  [blocker] Rexling's snout and Drako's muzzle are seated on the BELLY, not the mouth — in play they hang out of his underside as a bib and a pipe
    evidence: Rendered in play, at play size, in the state a buyer gets: scratchpad/snout/drako.png shows the dragon muzzle as a teal cylinder pointing straight down out of the bottom of the body with two orange dots at the far end — a hose, not a snout, and nowhere near the mouth. scratchpad/snout/rexling.png shows the dino snout as a flat, brighter-green lump with a hard edge across the bottom of the body — a bib. Same read on the shipped shop screenshot, store/07-skins.png (crops of both LEGENDARY rows). Cause, from source and exact: void3d.ts:1268 puts the muzzle cylinder at (0,-0.5,0.88) with a tip sphere at (0,-0.5,1.16) r=0.21, so its extremity is at (0,-0.5,1.37), |p| = 1.458 on a unit-radius body — it protrudes 0.46 radii past the surface, 20 degrees BELOW the +z axis, and dress.rotation.y (void3d.ts:1909) yaws it to face the camera, i.e. straight into the one direction the player is looking from. void3d.ts:1255 puts the dino jaw at (0,-0.56,0.8), extremity |p| = 1.379, 0.38 radii proud. The mouth group sits at y=-0.28 (void3d.ts:2104), so both parts are seated 0.22-0.28 units — 11-14% of the body's diameter — BELOW the mouth they are supposed to be. Second cause, colour: void3d.ts:1253/:1266 paint them MeshStandardMaterial in the skin's `mid` (0x55b850 / 0x2394a8, palette.ts:257/:262), but the fragment shader pulls the body toward `uAbyss` exactly where they sit (void3d.ts:258-261, the `core` term centred at N.xy = (0,-0.46)), and they are scene-lit while the body is self-lit — two lighting models inside one silhouette.
    why: These are the two cards labelled "LEGENDARY — A WHOLE NEW CHARACTER" at $2.99. A parent pays three dollars and their six-year-old gets a green ball with a pipe hanging out of its belly. It is also the only place in the game where the hero's silhouette is broken by something that reads as an error rather than as anatomy.

  [major] The hero takes no light from any world: the frame goes 3.9x darker and his body value moves 0.15%
    evidence: Controlled pair from the shipped set — same stage, same size, same skin, different world (both HUD-labelled CHOMPOSAURUS 7m). qa/_scratch/herohue.mjs finds the body disc and samples the 0.55r-0.85r ring, clear of every face feature and inside the rim stop: store/03-devouring.png (Maple, day) body HSV H=263.3 S=0.608 V=0.683 against a whole-frame mean luminance of 0.2357; store/04-lantern-market.png (Lantern Night) body H=262.9 S=0.586 V=0.684 against a frame luminance of 0.0601. The world is 3.9x darker; the hero is 0.1% brighter. 05-lantern-bathhouse V=0.578 and 06-gameday V=0.640 differ only because uStage and uPxR differ — his own growth moves him more than the sun does. Cause, from source: the body is a ShaderMaterial whose uniform list (void3d.ts:438-458) carries no ambient, sun, or fog term at all, and it is lit by a hardcoded view-space key, `vec3 L = normalize(vec3(-0.40, 0.60, 0.69))` (void3d.ts:~248), with `col *= mix(0.62, 1.22, key)`. He is a self-lit sticker, in every world, by construction.
    why: In shot 04 — an App Store screenshot — a daylight-lit purple ball is pasted onto a night market. The one thing that must be the same in all five worlds is his identity, not his exposure, and a child can see that he is not standing in the scene he is standing in.
    fix: NOT a rig change — WORLD_LIGHT's inert hemiI/exposure columns and RIG stay untouched (HANDS OFF), and this must not become another Lantern light-lift. Hero-local only: add one uniform `uWorldKey` (vec3, default 1,1,1) to makeVoidBody (void3d.ts:438) and multiply it into the two diffuse terms only — the uInner/uMid/uRim mix and the key — leaving `gal`, `uAbyss` and the pit alone, because the galaxy inside him emits and is the brand. The value is an authored per-world column, not arithmetic: deriving it from LIGHT.sun would tint him with Lantern's MOON (0xbfd4ff, cold) while the market around him is lantern-orange, which would be worse than today. So the experiment is: add a `heroKey` vec3 to each of the five WORLD_LIGHT entries (prototype3d.ts:677-739), pick the five values by eye against a render of the hero in each world, and put the sheet in front of the owner. That is a style decision with five numbers, and it belongs to a person, not to a formula.
    seeded draws: Zero.
    measure: New qa/heroworld.mjs (herohue.mjs is the working version): shoot the hero at a fixed stage and radius in all five worlds and report body-ring HSV against whole-frame mean luminance. Two bars — (a) body V must differ by >= 20% between the brightest world (Maple, frame lum 0.236) and the darkest (Lantern market, 0.060), and (b) body hue must stay within 8 degrees of the authored 263. (a) is deliberately tiny: the worlds are 3.9x apart, so 20% is a ~5% response — a floor under "he is lit by something", not a tuning target. (b) is the brand constraint that stops the fix eating the character. Today (a) reads 0.15% and fails; (b) reads 2.1 degrees and passes, and must keep passing.

WHAT TO PROTECT.

1. THE POSTER SET IS GENUINELY DIFFERENT AT THUMBNAIL SIZE. Squint-tested (firstglance/worlds-squint.png, a 14x box-downsample) and measured (qa/_distinct.mjs, 4x5 CIELAB mosaic): the minimum pairwise deltaE across all ten pairs of the five posters is 15.8 — every card reads as a different place with the type stripped off. All five assets are 641x858 (0.747), which is 3:4 to within 0.4%, so `background-size: cover` into the `.wArt` box (index.html:928) shows each painting essentially whole with no crop loss. Do not let anything crop or letterbox them.

2. THE PICKER FITS ONE SCREEN. Measured from the live DOM (qa/_lockshot.mjs): document.scrollHeight 932 against a 932 viewport at 430x932. Five worlds, no scroll, on the screen a pre-reader has to choose from. Every fix below is constrained to keep this — do not accept one that adds card height.

3. THE TYPE'S STROKE TREATMENT. index.html:958-962, `paint-order: stroke fill` plus a 2.5px dark stroke and two tight glows. It is the reason POWDER PASS survives over snow and PIRATE BAY over lagoon, and it is why my complaint below is occlusion and not legibility. qa/pickerfit.mjs already gates it properly and has retracted its own bad first bar in writing. 4. THREE OF THE FIVE ESTABLISHING SHOTS ARE EXCELLENT AND I WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE. ========================================================================
TEAM REVIEW — VERDICT NO-SHIP
========================================================================
WHAT IS GOOD:
Protect these — they are the reason this feels like a game and not a demo.

THE BITE CURVE ITSELF (`void3d.ts:1969-1974`). I measured it end to end on a forced size-class-up bite: maw 0.006 → 0.17 → 0.53 → 0.76 → **peak 0.853 at 206 ms** → 0.71 → 0.35 → shut by ~360 ms, and a second run peaking at 1.113. That is a real three-phase envelope — 45 ms of wind-up where the jaw barely parts, a spring open with an 11.8% overshoot (I evaluated `openEnv`: peak 1.1183 at mouthAge 0.225), and the `min(1, mouthT*8)` closing ease so the jaw never snaps. My finding #5 asks to re-grade the small end of `chomp()`; it does not touch this curve, and nothing should. It is better than most shipped mobile eat animations.

THE RETRIGGER RULE (`void3d.ts:1731-1746`). "A retrigger may extend the maw, never shrink it," with the failure it fixed written out in full. That is the correct invariant on the one action the game is made of, and it already has a fix in it — leave it alone.

THE MASS LAW (`void3d.ts:1806`). One clamp, `1.25 / (0.6 + dispR * 0.28)`, feeding the shader, the bob and the breathe. It is why a WORLD ENDER does not vibrate at the frequency of a marble. Enormous feel per line.

THE JELLY SLOSH (`void3d.ts:106`, `:1774`). `0.012 + uWobble * 0.06` against a `wob` term reaching 1.6 is ±11.5% of vertex displacement at full slosh, graded by bite size and decaying over 0.59 s, with ±1.9% always alive so the void is never static. The rivals get it too (`rivals.ts:1557`), which is why the family reads as the same species.

THE GROWTH SPRING (`void3d.ts:1769-1771`). 95/9.0 is ζ = 0.46 and a genuine 19% overshoot — the comment's own claim, and it checks out. `impulse()` shoving it on every meal is the right idea.

THE CAMERA, ALL OF IT. `camFollow` as its own state so a kick can never compound into a drift (`prototype3d.ts:9029-9039`). Lookahead smoothed off ACTUAL displacement rather than control velocity, clamped, and scaled by `camDist` so the lead stays a constant fraction of the frame from spawn to TITAN (`:9005-9025`). The steepening with size. Every smoothing term is `1 - exp(-k*dt)`, i.e. frame-rate independent by construction. And `camDist *= 1.07` on evolution (`:9099`) is a real camera answer that costs no shake — the world exhales. That is the one lens channel that survives the owner's order and it should be protected, not traded away.

THE ESTABLISHING SHOT (`prototype3d.ts:8967-8990`). Hold the subject on the landmark for the first quarter, hand over across the middle half, arrive settled so the controls go live on a still camera — and it turns shadows off for the dive because nobody can see them under a 3.4 s pull-back. That is a director's decision, executed.

THE FACE RIG. Eyes lit by the body's own key vector and its own 0.62–1.22 range rather than a gentler one; `wrapTo` seating each feature to the sphere normal; the face pushed clear of whatever envelope the body currently occupies (`:1958-1959`) so a slosh can never swallow the eyes; the caricature LOD driven off measured on-screen pixel radius; an AUTHORED blink cadence instead of `Math.random()`. I cropped it at 1.6× and it is the best asset in the repository.

THE HIT-STOP GATE (`prototype3d.ts:4926-4952`). Two rounds of dialling with the rate measured each time, and the reasoning left in the file. Finding #1 is about WHEN the freeze lands, not whether it should exist — the gate is right.

  [blocker] Hit-stop freezes the hero's face and lets the world's suction keep running — the landmark bite holds on a closed mouth

Measured with `qa/_mvduty.mjs` (written for this review, in the repo) on Maple, 41.7 sim s of play through the standard faceparity driver: 63 samples fell inside a hit-stop and the MEDIAN gape during them was **0.120** — exactly `MOODS.hungry.maw`, i.e. the idle mouth, not a bite. A forced size-class-up bite through `__eatNearest(0.6)` gives the whole timeline: maw 0.0061 → 0.0123 while `stopT>0`, then 0.17 → 0.53 → 0.76 → peak **0.853 at 0.206 s**. Meanwhile `:8881-8882` pulls magnetised props on `dt`, not `dtw`, so the one thing that does NOT hold its breath is the thing being eaten — while the already-captured prop's spiral at `:8818/:8823/:8837` correctly uses `dtw`.

Add `let stopArm = 0, stopPend = 0;` beside `stopT` (`prototype3d.ts:8104`); `hitStop(sec)` sets `stopPend = sec; stopArm = 0.15` instead of `stopT`; in `animate()` before `:8126` add `if (stopArm > 0) { stopArm -= dt; if (stopArm <= 0) stopT = Math.max(stopT, stopPend); }` and clear both on `ended`/`outroT`. 0.15 s is derived, not guessed: the wind-up ends at mouthAge 0.045 and `openEnv` first reaches 1.0 at mouthAge 0.157 (I ran the envelope). Do NOT touch `:8451-8461` — the void's STEERING staying on `dt` is a recorded owner-driven decision and this fix is consistent with it: that note is about the thumb, and `:8693` silently applied it to the face as well.

  [blocker] The evolution pop plays backwards: a 12.3% SHRINK is the whole gesture, and the 4.6% grow arrives 467 ms later
    evidence: `void3d.ts:1836-1839`. I evaluated it verbatim at dt=1/60: `uniformK` reaches its minimum **−0.1226 at t=0.150 s** and its maximum **+0.0462 at t=0.467 s**.     evidence: `void3d.ts:1781-1791`. `ringBurst` starts at 1 and decays at 0.55/s, and both the opacity and the radius ride `fadeEnv = sin(min(1, 1 - ringBurst) * π)`. If the duty cycle is still over bar after the regrade, the next lever is a ceiling on extension (`mouthT = Math.min(0.55, Math.max(mouthT, want))`), which caps a hoover spree without letting a small bite ever shrink a big one.

### Maple Falls' ground is a flat paint bucket — and it is 40% of the first frame
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/island.ts:718 (and :1730, :1972, :2645)

EVIDENCE — the base, and the only variation ever applied to it:
```
718:  g.fillStyle = hex(WORLD.meadow); g.fillRect(0, 0, TEX, TEX);
719:  // subtle grass mottling
720:  for (let i = 0; i < 4000; i++) {
721:    g.fillStyle = Math.random() < 0.5 ? 'rgba(120,201,78,0.16)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,0.035)';
722:    const x = Math.random() * TEX, y = Math.random() * TEX, r = rand(2, 6);
```
`WORLD.meadow` is `0x74c352` = (116,195,82). The mottle tint is (120,201,78) at **alpha 0.16** — a composited shift of (+0.6, +1.0, −0.6) out of 255, i.e. **below one 8-bit step**. 4000 arcs of radius 2–6 on a 3072² canvas is ~2% coverage. It is invisible by arithmetic before it is invisible by eye.

Then it is painted over anyway:
```
1730:    g.fillStyle = hex(col);
1731:    g.fillRect(x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0);
1732:  }
1733:  // forest gets a darker dappling; downtown a plaza tint already via pavement
```
Every `park` / `campus` / `fair` / `farm` / `strip` block is one opaque `fillRect`. The comment on 1733 promises a forest dapple; grep of the whole Maple bake (1737→2480) finds no `ellipse` or mottle pass on any green biome — the comment describes code that does not exist.

And the square in the photo — the spawn block — is the same:
```
1972:    g.fillStyle = '#8ddc63';
1973:    g.fillRect(pxW(gx0), pyW(gy0), pxW(gx1 - gx0) - pxW(0), pyW(gy1 - gy0) - pyW(0));
1977:    g.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.075)';
```
One flat fill plus five 7.5%-white mow stripes.

The runtime grain overlay cannot rescue it:
```
2645:    maple:   [0.45, 0.08, 0.00, 9],
2652:    lantern: [0.30, 0.30, 0.34, 7],
```
The 0.45 goes to the 140×-repeat layer, and the file's own comment at :2525-2534 proves that layer "mips to flat grey before it ever reaches the screen"; the layer that *does* resolve (34×) runs at 0.08; the coarse mottle is off. The code even records the measurement:
```
2625:  // it. Measured with qa/ground.mjs, Lantern (which does use
2626:  // it, at 0.34) carries 6x Maple's fine detail energy, 3.9x the mid and 2.7x
2627:  // the coarse, on triple the spread.
```
Compare what the *other* worlds got. Pirate Bay, island.ts:1010-1027:
```
1010:      for (let k = 0; k < 13000; k++) {
1013:        g.fillStyle = Math.random() < 0.5 ? 'rgba(28,24,16,0.11)' : 'rgba(255,250,232,0.13)';
1019:      for (let k = 0; k < 9000; k++) {
1027:          ? (Math.random() < 0.5 ? 'rgba(28,82,44,0.42)' : 'rgba(176,222,132,0.40)')
```
13,000 grain chips plus **9,000 grass-tuft strokes at alpha 0.40-0.42, each 26-62 world units long**. Powder gets 3,600 blobs plus a rim shade (:844-865). Maple — world 1, the level with no menu on run one — got 4,000 sub-1/255 specks that are then overpainted.

I measured the shipped frame itself (pure-node PNG decode of `qa/out/shippedlook/maple_firstlook.png`, high-pass detail energy at three radii):

| patch | mean | sd | detail r1 | r2 | r4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lawn, lower-left (prop-free) | 0.626 | 0.011 | **0.00126** | 0.00280 | 0.00501 |
| lawn, top-right | 0.547 | 0.020 | **0.00204** | 0.00381 | 0.00509 |
| plaza tan, same frame | 0.619 | 0.086 | 0.00536 | 0.01021 | 0.01645 |
| road asphalt, same frame | 0.386 | 0.144 | 0.00460 | 0.00915 | 0.01718 |

The grass carries **a quarter of the detail energy of the tan path lying right next to it**, and 0.00126 is at the noise floor of an 8-bit PNG.

WHY: This is the owner's complaint, literally. When a child taps MAPLE FALLS the biggest thing on the screen is a solid green rectangle with a solid tan rectangle beside it. Nothing about the surface says grass, mown lawn, packed earth or a place — it says "unfilled shape". A reviewer's screenshot pass reads it as a prototype in one glance, and it is the same surface for all three minutes.

FIX: One pass, in the bake, where Pirate already has it. After the biome block fills at :1732 (not before, or it gets overpainted), run a Maple grass pass in the same shape as :1019-1033 — a few thousand short strokes in two tones at ~0.35 alpha, clipped to the green biomes, plus ~150 large soft ellipses at ~0.15 for large-scale patchiness the camera can actually resolve. Second, retune `GRAIN.maple` off the diagnosed-dead mix: move weight from the 140× layer to the 34× layer (`[0.15, 0.30, …]`), which the existing `qa/_grainab.mjs` can A/B live via `groundMat.userData.grainU` without a rebuild. Do the same for `pirate` and `gameday` in the same commit — the "left on the mix they shipped with" note covers a mix the file's own arithmetic refutes.

GATE: `node qa/ground.mjs maple,pirate,gameday,lantern` — it already reports three-octave detail energy per world and would show Maple at ~1/6 Lantern before and within a stated margin after. Pin the tuning with `qa/_grainab.mjs` (fixed camera), which exists precisely because ground.mjs's void-driving has a noise floor bigger than the effect.

### Every scattered prop in Maple faces due north, and none of them varies in size
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/island.ts:5825 · src/proto3d/island.ts:4568 · src/proto3d/assets3d.ts:123

EVIDENCE — the three placers, and none of them applies a default:
```
island.ts:5817  const drop = (mesh, wx, wy, r, rotY?) => {
island.ts:5819    if (rotY !== undefined) mesh.rotation.y = rotY;

island.ts:4568  const place = (mesh, x3, z3, r) => {
island.ts:4571    mesh.position.set(x3, 0, z3);

assets3d.ts:123   if (opts.rotY) fb.rotation.y = opts.rotY;
```
`place()` has no rotation parameter at all. `drop()` and `glb()` leave `rotation.y = 0` when the caller omits it — and the Maple call sites overwhelmingly omit it:
```
5915:        dropGlb('parktree', tx, ty, 3.2, 7, makeTree);
5933:    for (const [px2, py2] of row(6700, 5830, 7300, 5830, 4)) drop(MS.makePlanter(), px2, py2, 0.9);
5969:        if (k % 4 === 0) drop(MS.makePlanter(), fx3, fy3, 0.9);
6004:      drop(MS.makeLawnSign(SIDE()), sx5, sy5, 0.55);
6028:      place(MS.makeLawnSign(side), hx + fx3 * 6.6 - sx3 * 2.2, hz + fz3 * 6.6 - sz3 * 2.2, 0.55);
```
Line 5933 is the planter row visible in the photograph: four barrels on a straight line, identical geometry, `rotation.y = 0` on all four. Line 5915 is every `parktree` — and `makeTree` places its canopy lobes at fixed asymmetric offsets (`R0*0.55, 5.4, R0*0.3` / `-R0*0.5, 5.6, -R0*0.25`), so **every tree in Maple presents the identical lobe arrangement to the identical camera angle**.

Scale: across the entire 900-line Maple populate block (5780-6676) there is exactly **one** `.scale` call, and it belongs to a specific landmark. No street prop is ever scaled.

WHY: This is absence #5 in its purest form and it is what the owner's eye caught as "bare minimum". Four planters, five newspaper boxes and six signs that are pixel-identical copies of each other read as *stamps*, not as objects a town put there. The eye names it "flat" before the mind names it "repeated".

FIX: Do **not** put a blanket random rotation in `place()`/`drop()` — that would spin storefronts off the kerb, benches away from the walk and the town hall off its axis. Add an opt-in at the scatter sites only, using the seeded stream so `qa/determ.mjs` still passes: `mesh.rotation.y = mr(0, Math.PI * 2)` for radially symmetric dressing (planters, bushes, flowers, trees, trash, hydrants) and `mesh.rotation.y = base + mr(-0.25, 0.25)` for the facing props (signs, news boxes) — the pattern already used correctly at :5928, :6098 and :6250. Add `mesh.scale.setScalar(mr(0.88, 1.14))` on the same set. Cost is zero: these are merged single-mesh props, so a group transform is free, and `mrnd()` (mainstreet.ts:28) keeps two loads pixel-identical.

GATE: New, and small — a probe that walks `window.__edibles`, buckets by builder signature (vertex count), and asserts that within any bucket of ≥4 instances the distinct `rotation.y` count and the `scale.x` spread both exceed a floor. Fails at 1 distinct rotation / 0 spread today. `qa/artaudit.mjs` is the right file to hang it on — it already traverses the scene for a material and silhouette inventory.

### There is no text on a single 3D prop in the game — every sign is a blank white bar
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/mainstreet.ts:590 · :606 · :1240 · :566

EVIDENCE — the signs in the photograph, exactly as authored:
```
mainstreet.ts:589    part(box(1.05, 0.72, 0.07), c, 0, 1.16, 0),
mainstreet.ts:590    part(box(0.78, 0.2, 0.1), WHITE, 0, 1.30, 0.02),                   // the banner line

mainstreet.ts:605    part(box(4.4, 2.4, 0.16), c, 0, 2.9, 0),
mainstreet.ts:606    part(box(3.4, 0.7, 0.2), WHITE, 0, 3.2, 0.05),
mainstreet.ts:607    part(box(2, 0.34, 0.2), WHITE, -0.6, 2.4, 0.05),

mainstreet.ts:1240    part(box(3.6, 1.4, 0.2), WHITE, 0, 14.2, 0.65),

mainstreet.ts:566    part(box(0.55, 0.6, 0.1), CREAM, 0, 1.7, 0.36),
```
The comments say what these are *for* — `// the banner line`, `// "THIS WAY"` — but they are white boxes. And there is no mechanism to fill them: `grep -rn "fillText\|strokeText" src/` returns **zero hits anywhere in `src/proto3d/`** except `void3d.ts:1111/1136` (the sleep "Z" billboard). Every other hit is in `src/game/`, the retired 2D shell. A `CanvasTexture` path exists and is used (`facadeTex`, island.ts:3120) — nothing routes text through it.

WHY: The photograph shows a red board with a blank white slab, a yellow board with a blank white slab, and three newspaper boxes with blank cream panels. To a reviewer that is the visual grammar of placeholder art. To a 6-year-old the town has signs that say nothing — and the newsroom, the game's whole differentiating thesis, never appears in the world it reports on.

FIX: One `signTex(text, bg, fg)` helper with a small `Map` cache next to `facadeTex` (island.ts:3119-3141) — a 256×64 canvas, one `fillText`, `t.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace`. Apply it to a plane sitting 0.01 proud of the board on the four builders above. Six or eight strings is enough (`FALL FAIR`, `THIS WAY`, `THE GAZETTE`, `MAPLE FALLS`, `VOTE DINKLE`, `PIE CONTEST`) picked with `mpick` so it stays deterministic — that also solves half the repetition finding for free, because the signs stop being identical.

GATE: `qa/artaudit.mjs` already counts "how many materials carry a map"; add an assertion that ≥N distinct mapped materials reach the GPU on Maple. It reads 0 for prop signage today.

### The lawn sign's rosette is authored 5 thousandths of a unit inside the board
SEVERITY: polish
AT: src/proto3d/mainstreet.ts:592

EVIDENCE:
```
589:    part(box(1.05, 0.72, 0.07), c, 0, 1.16, 0),
592:    part(new THREE.CircleGeometry(0.15, 12), WHITE, -0.28, 1.02, 0.03),
593:    part(new THREE.CircleGeometry(0.09, 10), c, -0.28, 1.02, 0.04),
```
`box(w,h,d)` is `BoxGeometry(w,h,d)` (mainstreet.ts:124) and `part(geo, col, x, y, z)` translates (island.ts:3535). The board is 0.07 deep at z=0, so its front face is at **z = +0.035**. The white outer disc sits at **z = +0.030** — behind the face, buried in the plank. The inner disc at +0.040 does clear it, but it is `c`, the board's own colour. Net visible result: nothing, on the one detail meant to break up the sign.

WHY: Small on its own, but this sign is placed hundreds of times across Maple (":584 There are hundreds of these"), and it is the reason each one reads as a bar on a rectangle rather than a poster.

FIX: `0.03` → `0.045` and `0.04` → `0.05`. Two characters.

GATE: New — a build-time assertion over the merged geometry's bounding boxes per part, or simply fold it into the signage probe above.

### The green half of the frame is six colours from the same hue
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/palette.ts:114 · src/proto3d/island.ts:4140 · src/proto3d/island.ts:3698

EVIDENCE:
```
palette.ts:114    foliage: [0x5dbe63, 0x4faa5a, 0x6cc86e],
island.ts:4140      : [0x6cc86e, 0x5db06a, 0x7ed57a]), 0.95, false));
```
Plus `meadow: 0x74c352`, `park: 0x9ae878`, `campus: 0x8fd06a`, and the square at `#8ddc63`. Every one of those is the same yellow-green hue family separated only by value. The bush palette even shares `0x6cc86e` with the tree palette exactly — bushes and trees are literally the same green.

And the tree's two-tone is weaker than it reads in source:
```
3697:  const base = pick(foliagePool());
3698:  const dark = new THREE.Color(base).multiplyScalar(0.7).getHex();
3699:  const light = new THREE.Color(base).multiplyScalar(1.28).getHex();
```
`Color(hex)` decodes to linear working space (the codebase states this itself at island.ts:3535: *"_pc.setHex() returns LINEAR values (three's ColorManagement converts from sRGB on the way in)"*), and `getHex()` re-encodes to sRGB. So ×1.28 and ×0.7 in linear are ×1.11 and ×0.85 **on screen**. For `0x6cc86e` the three canopy lobes land at green 171 / 200 / 224 — a ±13% ramp, softened further by the smooth-shaded normals. The canopy has no colour break at all, only a value ripple, which is why a 14×10 sphere cluster photographs as one balloon.

WHY: The owner's "bare minimum" verdict is a hue verdict as much as a texture one. The orange maples in the same frame read far better than the green trees for exactly this reason: `LEAF_A..D` + `LEAF_HERO` (mainstreet.ts:147-148) are five genuinely different hexes alternated per sphere (`i % 2 ? leaf : LEAF_HERO`, :1442), so each canopy has real internal variety. `makeTree` does not.

FIX: Two changes, both cheap. (a) Widen `PROPS.foliage` from three neighbouring greens to five that differ in **hue**, not value — a blue-green, a yellow-green, a sage — and shift the bush palette off the tree palette so a bush is not the same hex as a canopy. (b) Give `makeTree` the treatment `makeMapleTree` already has: pick two *different* entries from the pool for the lobes rather than deriving both from one via `multiplyScalar`, and if the scalar approach is kept, do it in sRGB space (`getHex()` → scale bytes → `setHex()`) so 0.7/1.28 mean what they look like they mean.

GATE: `qa/artaudit.mjs` already reports "hue spread, sampled from a real screenshot". Assert a minimum hue spread on Maple's frame; it is near-zero across the green mass today.

### The bush is one squashed sphere with no contact shading, and the flower bed is a hexagon with five dots
SEVERITY: minor
AT: src/proto3d/island.ts:4135 · src/proto3d/island.ts:4215

EVIDENCE:
```
4135:  const b = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(rand(1.4, 2.1), 12, 8),
4141:  b.position.y = 1; b.scale.y = 0.7; return b;

4215:  const parts = [part(new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(0.7, 0), 0x5db06a, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0.7, 1)];
4217:    parts.push(part(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.16, 6, 5), pick([...]), rand(-0.5, 0.5), 0.8, rand(-0.5, 0.5)));
```
`makeBush` returns a raw `Mesh` on a shared `stdMat`, not a `mergedProp` — so it never reaches `bakeContactAO`, which is called only from `mergedProp` (island.ts:3678: `if (mat !== PROP_GLOW_MAT) bakeContactAO(merged);`) and needs a `color` attribute the bush does not have (`3608: if (!pos || !col) return;`). It is the one prop class in the frame with no base darkening. `makeFlowers` — the five green hexagons in the photo — is a 20-face icosahedron plus five 0.16 spheres, and `IcosahedronGeometry` has a fixed orientation, so with no placement rotation every one is the identical hexagon at the identical angle.

WHY: In the photo the bushes are the flattest objects on screen after the ground — smooth green domes with no shadow side and no root. And "green hexagon with three dots" appears five times in one screenshot.

FIX: Route `makeBush` through `mergedProp([part(sphere, col, 0, 1, 0, 0,0,0, 1, 0.7, 1)])` so it inherits the vertex-colour AO the rest of the world already gets; add a second smaller offset lobe so the silhouette is not a perfect ellipse. For `makeFlowers`, raise the dot count from 5 to 7-9 and vary the base disc scale — it is the smallest edible in the game and there are hundreds of them.

GATE: `qa/shading.mjs` (flat/smooth/AO material census) plus the rotation-variety probe from finding 2.

### CONTACT — an honest empty
I went looking for props sitting on the ground like stickers and did not find it. `bakeContactAO` (island.ts:3605-3624, `AO_FRAC 0.34`, `AO_MAX 0.40`, squared falloff, proportional to each prop's own height) runs on every `mergedProp`, and the comment records the earlier fixed-band version being measured as invisible and replaced. `place()` (island.ts:4578-4585) gives everything that fails `shouldCast` a soft contact disc, and `shouldCast` (assets3d.ts:48) has a reasoned `r >= 4 || (h >= 6 && thin >= 0.8)` bar with the "sticks on the sand" failure written next to it. The sun runs a camera-tracking shadow frustum (`fitShadow`, prototype3d.ts:855-877) that halves texel size when the void is small. `PCFShadowMap` over `PCFSoftShadowMap` is deliberate and documented (prototype3d.ts:221-229). The two exceptions are named above: `makeBush` bypasses the AO path, and the hero itself is deliberately excluded (`qa/grounding.mjs` header). This area is in good shape and does not need work.

---

## The one change

**Give Maple Falls' grass a real surface.** It is the largest thing in the frame the owner photographed, it is the first thing every child ever sees in this game, and right now it is `fillRect` — measured at 0.00126 detail energy against 0.00536 for the tan path two inches away in the same picture, and 1/6 of Lantern's by the code's own recorded `qa/ground.mjs` run. Pirate Bay already has the exact pass that fixes it, twenty lines of it, at `island.ts:1010-1033`; Maple never received it. Nothing else in this list changes the perceived quality of that frame as much, and nothing else is as cheap: it is a bake-time canvas pass, zero runtime cost, zero draw calls, and `qa/ground.mjs` and `qa/_grainab.mjs` already exist to prove it landed.

Second, if there is room in the same pass: per-instance rotation and scale on the scatter (finding 2). One line per call site, free at runtime, and it removes the "stamped copies" read that is the other half of "bare minimum".

# FIRST GLANCE — the opening frame of all five worlds

## The instrument I used (and why the numbers below are what they are)

Everything here is derived from the shipped camera, not from a guess:

- `src/prototype3d.ts:538` — `const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(32, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 1, 1000);`
- `src/prototype3d.ts:8797` — `let targetDist = Math.min(340, Math.max(26, 38 * Math.pow(R / 0.9, 0.82)));` → at the spawn radius (`voidling.setRadius(0.9)`, `src/prototype3d.ts:2448`) that is **camDist 38**.
- `src/prototype3d.ts:553` — `const camOffset = new THREE.Vector3(0.62, 0.92, 0.62).normalize();`
- `ios/App/App/Info.plist:35-46` — `UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait` only, iPhone **and** iPad.
- `qa/shot.mjs:22` / `qa/hero.mjs:24` — `viewport: { width: 430, height: 932 }`.

`fov` in three.js is **vertical**. At aspect 430/932 the horizontal FOV is **15.1°**, not 32°. So the settled opening frame is a ground trapezoid roughly **8–14 units wide and 32 units deep** (≈ 366 u², ≈ 240 × 640 *world* units) centred on the void. I verified the model against a real shipped frame: `store/03-devouring.png` shows the void at "DEVOURER 7m", where the model predicts the hero at 26 % of screen width and the screenshot measures ≈ 31 % (the mesh renders slightly wider than the collision radius). It holds.

Two consequences drive most of what follows. **(a)** Nothing more than ~5–7 units left or right of the void is on screen at spawn — no landmark in any world is. So "what the level looks like at first glance" is decided almost entirely by the 2.2–3.6 s intro dive plus a very small patch of ground. **(b)** Screen-right is `(+x, −z)/√2` and screen-up is `(−x, −z)/√2` — the HANDOFF's "screen-up is not north" trap — and several authored opening compositions were written in world axes and never checked in screen axes.

## The per-world verdict

| world | intro | what the child sees in the first second | what the settled frame holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GAME DAY** | 3.4 s hold on the stadium ✔ | the bowl, centre frame, then a pull back into the lot | the tailgate rows — trucks/RVs/canopies at alternating headings (island.ts:5136-5142), the densest district measured in the game at 5.34 edibles/100u² (island.ts:4879) | **strongest** |
| **LANTERN NIGHT** | 3.6 s corridor hold on the bathhouse ✔ | lanterns receding to a lit building | inside LANTERN ROW, two lit stalls at ndc (−0.85, 0.12) and (0.43, −0.45), warm props on dark ground — the best figure-ground in the game | **second** |
| **POWDER PASS** | 3.5 s hold on the Lodge ✔ | the lodge on its hill over open white | ≈12 objects, ~10 of them the same white snow lump; the authored snack ring is off the right bezel | **third** |
| **PIRATE BAY** | 2.2 s — 320 u/s whip pan | motion across the island; the hotel never settles | open sand in DANCE COVE; stage at ndc 5.36, speaker stack at 1.41 — nothing authored in frame | **fourth** |
| **MAPLE FALLS** | **none** — 2.2 s dive onto the player's own feet | grass, then more grass | 10 of 49 square props: 4 protesters, a parking meter, an elm, a bench, 2 lawn signs, a news box | **weakest — and it is world 1** |

**Weakest opening: MAPLE FALLS**, and the reason is one field. `hero: null` at `src/prototype3d.ts:1191` means `if (introT > 0 && COPY.hero)` at `src/prototype3d.ts:8836` never fires, so the only world every player is guaranteed to see is the only world whose match opens on nothing in particular — with a hero landmark that already has its cue, its news line, its "GONE" banner and its Title-Case name filled in one row below. The compiler could not catch it because `null` is a legal value for a world that genuinely has no landmark, which was true of Maple *until the finale pass gave it one*.

## Is anything else thin at spawn, in the way Powder was?
No. Global densities are 3.80/100u² (Game Day), 4.85 (Lantern, post-pass), ~4.0 (Powder, post-hoover), 2.38 (Maple, post-verge-fill). Applied to the 366 u² opening frame that is 9–20 objects everywhere — nobody is starved. Powder's problem is not count, it is **sameness**; Pirate's and Maple's is not count, it is **that the composed thing is outside the frame**.

## The world picker
The chrome is sound: `overflow-y: auto` on `.metaScr` (index.html:1326) means the fifth card scrolls into reach, the 3:4 poster + footer-band type (index.html:927-940) keeps the art off the hero, `.wBest` gives a returning child a number to beat, and locked cards keep their poster desaturated with a stated unlock. Two small notes, neither worth a finding on its own: `index.html:966-976` styles `.wCard.lock` and `#worlds .wCard.lock .wArt`, but the JS only ever writes `.locked` (prototype3d.ts:5562) — those rules and the `document.querySelectorAll('.wCard.lock')` blocks at prototype3d.ts:5621-5629 are dead. And the cards do promise what the worlds deliver — Maple's poster shows a bandstand, a courthouse-square hall, shopfronts, a fountain and trees, and all five of those are authored in `island.ts`'s SQUARE block. The gap between poster and world is not the art. **It is the five seconds of generic splash art in between, and the fact that Maple's frame does not contain a single one of the things its own poster shows.**
