## KIDS SAFETY, PRIVACY, AND APPLE'S RULES — audit findings

**The telemetry layer itself is in good shape and I could not break it.** Before the findings, the enumeration you asked for, because it is the answer to the headline question and it is a *pass*:

Exactly one external host is contacted by the shipping bundle: `https://uzkzuxwykajzoicuxhic.supabase.co/functions/v1/ingest-events` (`src/game/analytics.ts:8`). It is the only `fetch()` to a non-relative URL in `src/` — `audio3d.ts:370/568/604` are same-origin, `src/index.css:1`'s Google Fonts import is reachable only from `src/main.tsx`, which is not a rollup input (`vite.config.ts:315` — `main:` is `index.html` and nothing else). No ad SDK, no third-party analytics, no crash reporter, no remote config. `navigator` is touched three ways only — `vibrate` (10×), `serviceWorker`, `clipboard` — plus `hardwareConcurrency`/`deviceMemory` inside `telemetry.ts:107-110`. No `randomUUID`, no `crypto.*`, no `uuid`, no device id anywhere in `src/`. The only text input in the whole app is the parental gate's numeric box (`index.html:1843`). The payload is `{session_id, app_version, platform, events[]}` (`analytics.ts:48`), `user_id` is genuinely absent, `vd_uid` is actively deleted (`analytics.ts:38`), and `logEvent` returns early when consent is off (`analytics.ts:90`). Every cash purchase path and RESTORE goes through `askGrownUp()`; every GEM spend does not and never falls through toward a payment sheet (`prototype3d.ts:7089-7092`, `7869-7873`). There is no urgency or scarcity copy anywhere. `mealOf()` (`prototype3d.ts:3506-3536`) really does prevent a person appearing in a headline. **Those are all clean, and I checked each one against the file rather than assuming.**

What follows is what is not.

### The parental gate is brute-forceable, and it is the *only* thing protecting the analytics switch
SEVERITY: major
AT: `src/prototype3d.ts:6687-6692`

EVIDENCE — the wrong-answer branch:
```
    } else {

`gateAns` is set once inside `askGrownUp()` (`:6672`) and is not re-rolled here; there is no counter, no delay, no lockout. `qa/_gatebrute.mjs:1-5` already recorded the analysis:

// SCRATCH — CAN A CHILD BRUTE-FORCE THE PARENTAL GATE?
// The gate (prototype3d.ts:3475) re-rolls its sum only inside askGrownUp().

### The client's IP reaches Supabase with every batch, and the policy's analytics paragraph denies collecting it
SEVERITY: major
AT: `src/game/analytics.ts:58-62` · `public/privacy.html:71-76`

EVIDENCE — the transmission:
```
    void fetch(INGEST_URL, {
      method: 'POST', keepalive: useBeacon,
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${ANON_KEY}`, apikey: ANON_KEY },
      body,
    }).catch(() => {});
```
and the disclosure, in the section headed "Anonymous statistics":
```
  <p>There is no persistent identifier of any kind. ... We do not collect the advertising identifier, precise screen dimensions, device model,
  IP-based location, or contacts. These statistics are stored by our hosting provider,
  Supabase, purely so we can query them; they are never sold, never shared for advertising,
  and never used to identify a person.</p>
```
The page *does* disclose IP for the CDN, in a different section (`privacy.html:85-89`, "Hosting and artwork") — so the omission is specifically in the analytics paragraph, the one a regulator would read.

WHY: An HTTPS POST unavoidably discloses the source IP to Supabase, and Supabase edge functions log request metadata by default. Under COPPA an IP address collected from a child is personal information; Apple's Kids rule, which `analytics.ts:26-29` quotes correctly, bars sending *device information* to a third party. The policy's own wording — "We do not collect ... IP-based location" — reads as a denial that the transmission occurs. It is defensible if the function drops it, and indefensible if it does not, and **nobody in this repo can tell which**: there is no edge-function source anywhere in the tree (`find` for `supabase/`, `functions/` returns nothing outside `analytics/funnels.sql`).

FIX: Two steps in order. (1) Check the deployed `ingest-events` function and Supabase's log retention for that project; if the IP is retained, drop it at the function and turn off request logging. (2) Either way, amend the analytics paragraph to say plainly that "like any internet request, our statistics server sees the IP address your connection came from; we do not store it, log it, or use it for anything." Vagueness here costs more than the sentence does.

GATE: not a browser probe — a documented one-time check recorded in `APPSTORE.md` beside the analytics bullet, plus `qa/privacy.mjs` asserting the policy page contains the word "IP" inside the statistics section (a text assertion, but it catches the paragraph being rewritten back).

It is not only that block: query 1 (the daily picture, the one the owner will actually open on launch day) counts `distinct user_id` and `first_open`, both of which the client stopped sending, and the 10-line funnel at `:116-125` groups every step by `user_id`. On day one the owner opens his dashboard and every column reads 0 or 1. That is a bad morning for a person who was promised numbers.

FIX: (1) Purge `user_id` from `vd_events` (or drop the column) and note the date in `APPSTORE.md` beside the analytics bullet — "no identifier is collected, and the historic ones were deleted on YYYY-MM-DD" is the sentence that makes `privacy.html`'s children's-privacy section true. (2) Rewrite queries 1 and the funnel onto `session_id`, and put a one-line header on each saying what it can and cannot answer without an identifier.

GATE: no probe; this is a data-and-docs action. `qa/privacy.mjs`'s static half can assert `analytics/funnels.sql` contains no `user_id` reference outside a block explicitly marked as a historical record.

### Unbounded third-party error text leaves the device

```
      track('iap_init_failed', { why: String(e).slice(0, 120) });

WHY: Every other field in every one of the ~45 `track()` call sites is a number, a boolean, or a game-authored string — I walked all of them. These two are the exception: 120 characters of whatever `cordova-plugin-purchase` throws. StoreKit error text can carry a product id, a URL, a file path, or account-state wording, none of which anybody has enumerated. It is small, it is opt-in, and it is still the one field in this build that cannot be described in a privacy answer, which is a problem when you are about to write a privacy answer. `prototype3d.ts:5627`'s `card: (c as HTMLElement).dataset.name || c.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 24)` is the same shape but bounded to the game's own copy, so it is fine.

GATE: `qa/privacy.mjs` static half — assert no `track(` call site in `src/` passes an expression containing `String(e)` or `e.message`.

### Opting in mid-session loses that day's session-shape events permanently
SEVERITY: minor
AT: `src/game/analytics.ts:116-121`

EVIDENCE:
```
  const today = new Date().toDateString();
  if (lsGet('vd_last_open_day') !== today) {
    lsSet('vd_last_open_day', today);
    logEvent('day_open', {});
  }
  logEvent('app_open', {});
```

WHY: `bootAnalytics` runs at import (`telemetry.ts:25`), before any parent could have consented. It writes `vd_last_open_day = today` unconditionally, then calls `logEvent`, which drops the event (`:90`). When the parent later turns stats on, `day_open` for that day is gone — and because the key was already stamped, it will not fire on a relaunch the same day either. Same for `app_open` and for `device` (`telemetry.ts:106-111`, which also runs at import). The consented session reports matches with no session frame around them. Nobody's privacy is harmed; the data the owner opted in for is just quietly incomplete on day one, which is the day he will look.

FIX: Move the `lsSet` inside the enabled branch, or have `setAnalyticsEnabled(true)` call a `bootAnalytics` re-run guarded by a separate flag.

GATE: `qa/privacy.mjs` — boot with consent off, toggle it on through the gate, and assert the first transmitted batch contains `app_open` and `device`.

It is a last-words joke; adults get it instantly, and a six-year-old is being asked to hold "the person is going to die" in a 4+ app whose stated rating answer is "nobody is hurt, nobody dies" (`APPSTORE.md:325-326`). `generic` is the fallback pool, so it fires on any biome without its own. Everything else in these pools I checked and would defend — `zoo`'s "the lions are LOOSE!!", `forest`'s "BEAR! no. BIGGER!!", `oldtown`'s "get the KIDS off the wall!!" are all inside cartoon convention.

---

**Areas I checked and found genuinely nothing.** Third-party SDKs, ad networks and remote fetches beyond the one Supabase endpoint. Persistent identifiers, device fingerprinting, and IDFA — the fingerprint really was collapsed to one three-value tier and I verified the code, not the comment. Outbound links: exactly one (`mailto:` in the policy iframe), correctly gated; `window.open` appears nowhere. `Info.plist` declares no camera, mic, location, contacts, photo or tracking permission, and `App.entitlements` is empty by deliberate decision. IAP gating: every cash path and RESTORE raises `askGrownUp()`, every gem path does not, and the shortfall messages route to play (`prototype3d.ts:7090`, `7870`) and never toward a payment sheet. No pressure-to-buy copy — no urgency, scarcity, countdown, "best value" or "limited time" anywhere in `index.html`, `prototype3d.ts` or `hats.ts`. `public/sw.js` caches same-origin only (`:56`). The two newsroom files the safety scanner misses are, when read by hand, clean. And `mealOf()` really does stop the paper ever printing that it ate a person.

## Findings — performance and memory against the §7 budget

I read the loop and the per-frame callees rather than timing anything. Three things I expected to find are **not** there, and I say so plainly at the end.

### The frame is O(rivals × edibles) with no spatial index anywhere
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/rivals.ts:1542, src/prototype3d.ts:8665, src/prototype3d.ts:8762, src/prototype3d.ts:913

EVIDENCE — the rival "passing bite" scan, inside `for (const rv of rivals)` (rivals.ts:820) inside `update()` (rivals.ts:688), with no cooldown and no reject before the per-element work:
```

1543            if (eaten(e.mesh) || e.radius > rv.r * EAT_RATIO || e.radius < minPassing) continue;
1544            const dx = e.mesh.position.x - rv.x, dz = e.mesh.position.z - rv.z;
1545            if (dx * dx + dz * dz < (rv.r + e.radius * 0.6) ** 2) {
```
Un-joined rivals do skip it — rivals.ts:853 `} else continue;   // not on the island yet` — so the cost *ramps in* as the family arrives (`slots = [rand(2,5), rand(9,15), rand(19,27), rand(30,40), rand(42,54)]`, rivals.ts:490).

And three more full passes of the same array, every frame, in `animate()`:
```
8665  for (const e of edibles) {
8666    if (!started || ended || paused) break;
```
```
8761  // decay prop shakes (too-big objects wobble as the void passes through)
8762  for (const e of edibles) {
8763    const ud = e.mesh.userData;
8764    if (ud.shakeT > 0) {
```
```
 913  for (const e of edibles) {          // fadeOccluders, called at prototype3d.ts:9148
 914    if (e.eaten) continue;
```
`grep -rn "spatial\|bucket\|cellFor" src/` returns nothing but two unrelated comments. Confirmed counts: Maple 5,790 edibles, Powder 4,536 (AAA-BRIEF:1057-1068); Game Day is the heaviest world.

WHY: on Maple with the full cast joined that is 5 × 5,790 + 3 × 5,790 ≈ **46,000 edible visits per frame, ~2.8 M/s at 60 fps**, and the peak coincides exactly with the moment the budget already concedes ground — tier B "60 fps, dips to 45 under the finale" and tier C's 30 fps. The 8665 loop pays a `Math.hypot` on every entry before any reject; the 8762 loop touches all ~5,800 userData objects to service the handful with a live `shakeT`. A child sees the last third of every match run worse than the first third, on the world the store screenshots come from.

FIX: one static uniform grid over `edibles`, built once beside `bakeContactShadows()` (they already walk the same array) with a separate small list for `userData.mover` props, and have rivals.ts:1542/1522/1074 and prototype3d.ts:913/8665 query cells within their own reach instead of the whole array. Smallest independent win if the grid is too much for one change: keep an `active` array of props with `shakeT > 0` so 8762 is O(shaking) not O(5,790).

GATE: `qa/hitch.mjs` — it reports the ratio shape rather than absolute fps, which is what transfers off swiftshader; the pre-fix build should show the median frame cost climbing as `rivals.list.filter(r=>r.joined).length` goes 1→5. `qa/lnperf.mjs` extended to print elapsed main-thread ms per `rivals.update` call at t=5 s vs t=120 s would fail before and pass after.

### The skin preview allocates ~1.3 MB of garbage per frame and stalls the GPU pipeline per frame
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:7631-7638

EVIDENCE:
```
7631        renderer.readRenderTargetPixels(prevRT!, 0, 0, PREV_S, PREV_S, buf);
7632        renderer.setRenderTarget(null);
7633        if (ctx) {
7634          const img = ctx.createImageData(PREV_S, PREV_S);
7635          for (let y = 0; y < PREV_S; y++) {
7636            img.data.set(buf.subarray((PREV_S - 1 - y) * PREV_S * 4, (PREV_S - y) * PREV_S * 4), y * PREV_S * 4);
7637          }
7638          ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
```
This is the body of `frame()`, re-armed every frame at prototype3d.ts:7596 `prevRaf = requestAnimationFrame(frame);`. Size:
```
7583    if (!PREV_S) PREV_S = Math.round((host.getBoundingClientRect().width || 190) * DPR);
7290  const DPR = Math.min(3, Math.max(1, window.devicePixelRatio || 1));
```
index.html:1066 `#skinPrev .spOrb { width: min(190px, 42vh); … }` → on any iPhone, PREV_S = 570.

WHY: `createImageData(570,570)` is a fresh 1,299,600-byte `Uint8ClampedArray` **every frame** — ~78 MB/s of garbage on a build whose whole heap ceiling is 450 MB, plus 570 `subarray` objects per frame. `readRenderTargetPixels` is a synchronous `glReadPixels`: it flushes and blocks the main thread on the GPU, every frame. And nothing pauses the main world — `animate()` keeps rendering the full scene plus the bloom chain behind the modal. A six-year-old opens the shop, taps a character to look at it, and leaves it open; that is the state the game is least able to survive.

FIX: hoist `img` out of `frame()` — create the `ImageData` once beside `buf` (line 7593) and reuse `img.data` — and drive the turntable off the same `buf`/`prevRT` at a fixed 30 Hz rather than every frame. That is two lines and removes ~90% of both costs.

GATE: `qa/heap.mjs` with a new step that opens `#skinPrev`, holds it 5 s, and asserts `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize` growth under a cap; fails hard pre-fix. `qa/hitch.mjs` pointed at the shop would show the p99/median ratio blow out pre-fix.

### Item #47 answered: two decoded tracks stay resident for the session, and `stopMusic()` never releases either
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/audio3d.ts:606, src/proto3d/audio3d.ts:3967-3982

EVIDENCE — decode, assigned to the channel and held:
```
 606          ch.buf = await c.decodeAudioData(await r.arrayBuffer());
 607          ch.loop = loopFor(u);
```
`preloadMusic()` decodes **both** channels on every page load (audio3d.ts:3812-3814):
```
3812      const first = straightIn ? () => preload(themeCh, urls) : () => preload(menuCh, [MENU_URL]);
3813      const second = straightIn ? () => preload(menuCh, [MENU_URL]) : () => preload(themeCh, urls);
3814      void first()?.then(second, second);
```
and `stopMusic()` stops sources but never clears the buffer:
```
3974      themeCh.wanted = false;
3975      stopLoop(themeCh, 1.2);
```
`grep -n "buf = null" src/proto3d/audio3d.ts` → nothing.

**Answer to the tracker question:** exactly **two** at once (`menuCh` + `themeCh`), never more, because a world switch is a full page reload (prototype3d.ts:5589-5590 `localStorage.setItem('voidAutoPlay','1'); location.href = location.pathname;`) — so no previous world's track survives a switch. But neither is ever released within a session. Sizes at 128 kbps: `powder.mp3` 3,585,296 B ≈ 224 s, `gameday.mp3` 3,254,444 B ≈ 203 s, `menu.mp3` 2,254,508 B ≈ 141 s. Decoded to stereo f32 at an iOS 48 kHz context: **powder ≈ 86 MB, gameday ≈ 78 MB, menu ≈ 54 MB — 132–140 MB resident, permanently.**

WHY: this sits *outside* the JS heap the 450 MB budget measures, so Game Day's "~446" understates the real footprint by roughly 30%. On iOS that is total process footprint and it is what jetsam kills on. An App Store reviewer on an older device backgrounding and returning is the likely trigger.

FIX: release `menuCh.buf = null` when a match starts (it re-preloads during the match for the results screen with time to spare), and `themeCh.buf = null` in `stopMusic()` when returning to the menu. That halves resident PCM to one track. Cheaper still, if a re-decode on PLAY AGAIN is unacceptable: keep only the world track and let the menu use the synth bed, which already exists as the 404 fallback.

GATE: `qa/journey.mjs` already walks gate → picker → shop → book → match; add an assertion on `__audio` reporting `themeCh.buf`/`menuCh.buf` non-null count ≤ 1 at any point after the first match starts. Fails today at 2.

### 84% of the heap budget is CPU-side vertex data the GPU already has, and nothing releases it
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/proto3d/island.ts:3782-3787 (`mergedProp`), and the absence of any `onUpload` in `src/`

EVIDENCE — the merge, and the four attributes it keeps:
```
3776    if (pg.getAttribute('uv')) pg.deleteAttribute('uv');
3777    if (!pg.getAttribute('aGloss')) {
3778      const n = pg.getAttribute('position').count;
3779      pg.setAttribute('aGloss', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Uint8Array(n), 1, true));
3780    }
3781  }
3782  const merged = mergeGeometries(parts, false)!;
```
`qa/heap.mjs`'s own header states the consequence: *"37 bytes a vertex, so 111 bytes a triangle — and three keeps the CPU-side copy alive for the life of the page unless something releases it. Nothing does: there is no onUpload anywhere in src/."* Verified: `grep -rn "onUpload" src/` returns zero hits. AAA-BRIEF:180 has the measurement: *"Game Day already sits at ~376 MB of vertex buffers inside a ~446 MB heap."*

WHY: 376 of 446 MB — the entire margin under the 450 MB ceiling and then some — is a duplicate of data already uploaded to the GPU. Nothing in this build reads it back: `grep -rn "Raycaster" src/prototype3d.ts src/proto3d/*.ts` returns nothing, input is a virtual stick, and props are never picked. This is why no world has room for anything and why §5's checklist item 9 has stood open.

FIX: in `mergedProp`, after `bakeContactAO(merged)` and an explicit `merged.computeBoundingSphere()`, set `onUploadCallback` on each attribute to null its `array`. Bounding spheres must be computed first — that is the one thing three still needs the array for (frustum culling), and computing it eagerly is a one-liner. One change site covers every merged prop in five worlds.

GATE: `qa/heap.mjs` already prints both halves (admitted JS heap and geometry resident in the scene graph counted from the buffers). Pin a threshold — Game Day heap ≤ 200 MB — and it fails on HEAD, passes after.

### No shader warm-up, and the shadow programs compile on the exact frame the child gets control
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:8808-8811

EVIDENCE:
```
8808        if (introShadow === null) { introShadow = renderer.shadowMap.enabled; renderer.shadowMap.enabled = false; sun.castShadow = false; }
8809        if (introT <= 0 && introShadow !== null) {
8810          renderer.shadowMap.enabled = introShadow; sun.castShadow = introShadow; introShadow = null;
8811        }
```
Restored on the same frame the controls go live (prototype3d.ts:8812-8814 `if (introT <= 0 && firstRun && !dragTaught) { … dragTaught = true; …}`). `grep -rn "renderer.compile\|compileAsync\|prewarm" src/` → **zero hits anywhere in the project.** The cost of crossing this boundary is documented in this file, at prototype3d.ts:1044-1049: *"flipping shadowMap.enabled invalidates every material and rebuilds ~45 shader programs across a 10,869-mesh scene. Measured: a 1,677 ms frame and 3,190 ms of extra work."*

I checked the mechanism in the installed dependency rather than assuming it. `sun.castShadow = false` changes `numDirectionalShadows`, which bumps `state.version` (three.module.js:8841-8848), which forces `needsProgramChange` for every lit material (three.module.js:18386). **The mitigating detail** — and it is why this is major, not blocker — is that r185 keeps a per-material `programs` Map (three.module.js:18185-18213) and does *not* release the outgoing program, so this is a **first-page-load** cost, not a per-match one, and the intro's toggle incidentally pre-warms the shadowless set that the quality ladder's rung 3 later needs.

WHY: on the first match of a page load — which, on the world-switch path, is the *only* match on that page load — the shadow-enabled program set for everything currently on screen compiles at t = 3.4 s. That is the frame the establishing shot lands, the drag lesson appears and the thumb becomes live. It is the seam absence #6 names, and the game hitches in it.

FIX: behind the boot cover, immediately before `animate()` (prototype3d.ts:9226), call `renderer.compile(scene, camera)` twice — once with `sun.castShadow = false`, once with it true — restoring the flag afterwards. Both program sets then exist before the curtain lifts, and both the intro toggle and every future ladder crossing are free.

GATE: `qa/shaderstall.mjs` — it already wraps the live context and counts `linkProgram` per frame. Assert **zero** links after `__matchState().t > 0`. Fails today with a burst at the end of the intro.

### Frame-rate-dependent constants at 120 Hz — the named list for tracker #39
SEVERITY: minor (as shipped to iOS) / major (web build)
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:9200, src/prototype3d.ts:8332, src/proto3d/life.ts:3665, src/prototype3d.ts:8435

EVIDENCE — the loop has **no frame limiter of any kind**: `grep -rn "setAnimationLoop\|maxFPS\|frameCap" src/prototype3d.ts` returns nothing, and the loop re-arms unconditionally at prototype3d.ts:9211 `requestAnimationFrame(animate);`. The constants that are not delta-corrected:

1. **Shadow refresh rate** — prototype3d.ts:9200
```
  if ((shadowFrame++ & 1) === 0) renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true;
```
Counted in *frames*, not seconds. At 60 Hz the shadow pass runs 30×/s; at 120 Hz it runs 60×/s. Pure doubled cost — the shadow pass is a second full-scene draw — for detail no eye resolves at 120 Hz.

2. **The steering time constant** — prototype3d.ts:8331-8333
```
    const k = Math.min(1, dt * (driving ? 11 - 3.5 * wgt : 4.5) * iceK);   // 91ms snappy tiny → 133ms weighty huge
    velX += (tvx - velX) * k;
    velZ += (tvz - velZ) * k;
```
A linear `dt*C` lerp, not `1 - exp(-C·dt)`. At 60 Hz k = 0.183 against a true 0.167; at 120 Hz k = 0.0917 against 0.0876. The response constant shifts ~4.5% between refresh rates — small, but it is the one verb the game has, and the brief's "60-tuned" warning is about exactly this. (Contrast prototype3d.ts:8100 `const dk = Math.pow(0.9, dt * 60);`, which is exact — the file already knows the right idiom.)

3. **Volleyball spin** — life.ts:3665
```
              ball.rotation.x += 0.11; ball.rotation.z += 0.07;
```
Per frame. Double speed at 120 Hz — and, because it is inside a mover subject to the distance stagger (life.ts:5463-5466), it also spins at ¼ speed when far away and 4× that when you approach. Cosmetic, but visible.

4. **Dead-end velocity bleed** — prototype3d.ts:8435
```
          velX *= 0.86; velZ *= 0.86;
```
Per frame in the inside-corner fallback. At 120 Hz the void bleeds speed twice as fast per second when wedged.

Everything else I checked is correct: `farPhase`'s stagger compensates with `dt * 2` / `dt * 4` (life.ts:5464-5469); `fovKick *= Math.pow(0.002, dtRaw)`; the quality ladder is on `dtRaw` wall time (prototype3d.ts:9166); the music watchdog is on `performance.now()`; the stall detector scales its threshold by `Math.max(0.4, dt * 60)`.

WHY: the shipped **iOS** build is protected by accident, not design — `ios/App/App/Info.plist` has no `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` key, so WKWebView is capped at 60 Hz on ProMotion. The **Vercel web build** in mobile Safari on an iPhone 13+ is not, and neither is any 120/144 Hz desktop. There the game does double the work, doubles the shadow pass, and drifts on the four constants above.

FIX: gate the loop to 60 Hz — accumulate `dtRaw` and skip the body (not the `requestAnimationFrame`) when less than ~15.5 ms have elapsed. That single change fixes all four at once and halves power draw on ProMotion. Then, independently, change 9200 to a wall-clock accumulator and 8332 to `1 - Math.exp(-C * dt)`.

GATE: no probe covers this today; the probe is the first deliverable. `qa/_ratecheck.mjs`: run a match with `requestAnimationFrame` shimmed to fire at 120 Hz, and assert that shadow-map updates per *second*, and the void's distance travelled per second under a constant stick, match the 60 Hz run within 2%. Fails on HEAD for both.

---

## Where I found nothing

- **Hot-loop allocation.** `sed -n '7971,9215p' src/prototype3d.ts | grep -c "new THREE"` → **0**. A scripted scan of every `update(dt…)` body in life.ts, rivals.ts, void3d.ts, newsroom.ts and prototype3d.ts found exactly one allocating call, life.ts:5483 `const near = peds.filter(…)`, and it is behind a ~2 s cooldown. `fx.ts` pools 12 rings and reuses one `shakeVec`. Contact shadows are a single `InstancedMesh` (prototype3d.ts:2527). The puff system writes into pre-allocated `Float32Array`s. The clock chip is change-detected (prototype3d.ts:8007-8010). This is genuinely careful code and I could not fault it.
- **Timer and listener leaks.** Every synth score guards its pump — `if (mapTimer) clearInterval(mapTimer);` (audio3d.ts:2391) and the same in `startTropical`, `startGameday`, `startLantern`, `startPowder`, `startSynth`. No `addEventListener` is registered inside `beginMatch`/`resetMatch`/`launchWorld`. Nothing accumulates across PLAY AGAIN there.
- **Mid-match texture uploads.** I expected rival skins to upload 1024² PNGs when the family joins. They do not: all five family skins (`univoid`, `rexling`, `kingvoid`, `drako`, `shadowninja`, palette.ts:252-259) are palette-only with no `tex` field, so `makeRivalMesh`'s loader branch (rivals.ts:281-296) never runs for them. Withdrawn before I wrote it down.
- **The quality ladder's absolute thresholds.** `avg < 46` / `avg > 57` (prototype3d.ts:9168-9170) look refresh-rate-naive but are correct against a 60 fps target on a 120 Hz panel in every case I worked through. Not a finding.

## One off-lens item I will not leave unsaid

`ios/App/App/Info.plist:10` reads `<string>VOIDLING</string>` for `CFBundleDisplayName`. HANDOFF §1 settles the home-screen label as **World Ender**, set via `capacitor.config.ts` `appName` — and a hard-coded `CFBundleDisplayName` overrides it. "Voidling" is the live App Store product the rename exists to avoid. Outside my lens, but it ships the collision to the home screen.

COVERAGE: docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/AAA-BRIEF.md (§2, §4.1, §5, §6, §7 performance budget and ledger), qa/README.md, src/prototype3d.ts (157-229, 362-397, 892-1071, 1073-1082, 2227, 2443-2540, 4759-4777, 5087-5200, 5589-5615, 6015-6220, 7290-7340, 7440-7650, 7971-9228), src/proto3d/fx.ts (whole file), src/proto3d/audio3d.ts (192-700, 770-790, 1640-1656, 2382-2398, 3640-3700, 3780-3830, 3960-4010), src/proto3d/rivals.ts (262-300, 375-500, 640-870, 1060-1090, 1500-1560), src/proto3d/life.ts (1976-2030, 3290-3320, 3640-3675, 4240-4290, 4810-4835, 5400-5541), src/proto3d/island.ts (585-640, 3020-3120, 3740-3820), src/proto3d/palette.ts (140-272), src/proto3d/telemetry.ts (73-93), src/proto3d/music-manifest.json, src/proto3d/bubbles.ts (grep), index.html (1066, 1371-1373, 1906), ios/App/App/Info.plist, qa/heap.mjs, qa/lnperf.mjs, qa/shaderstall.mjs, qa/shadowcost.mjs, qa/qualcost.mjs, qa/hitch.mjs, qa/journey.mjs, qa/propcount.mjs, node_modules/three/build/three.module.js (8014-8055, 8800-8850, 18150-18240, 18378-18400), public/assets/music/, public/assets/audio/, public/assets/hf/.

# FLUIDITY AND FEEL — audit of HEAD (`0dd4fb6`, `main`)

Read-only. Every line below was opened. Where I claim a number I computed it from the shipped constants; the arithmetic is shown.

## PART 1 — THE BITE: the channel census

One ordinary bite runs `capture()` at `src/prototype3d.ts:4765`. **Every channel below fires on the same frame, inside one function call — there is no stagger anywhere in the bite.**

| # | channel | line | fires for |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | prop toppled toward the hole (`e.spin.set`) | 4780 | every bite |
| 2 | prop's contact shadow retired | 4769 | every bite |
| 3 | hero radius spring target + `impulse()` shove | 4795, 4797 | every bite |
| 4 | mouth envelope `chomp(bite)`, graded 0.47→1.00 | 4917 | every bite |
| 5 | absorb sparks, count graded `3 + min(9, r*2.2)`, tinted from the prop's own vertex colours | 4906 | every bite |
| 6 | score floater `+N` | 4948 | every bite |
| 7 | combo increment + 1.6 s window | 4828 | every bite |
| 8 | audio `pop()` — 3 synth layers, pentatonic ladder, depth graded on meal size | 4955 | every bite (75 ms limiter) |
| 9 | haptic `buzz(8 | 15)` | 4955 | every bite (70 ms limiter) |
| 10 | `audio.voice('yum')` + tinted shockwave ring + second puff | 4911–4915 | `r > 2` |
| 11 | `CHOMP!` float + `bigEat()` + `buzz(30)` | 4954 | `r > voidR`, 7 s cooldown |
| 12 | **hitStop** 55–105 ms | 4820 | `bite > 0.55 && r > 1.1 && kitCd ≤ 0` |
| — | `camPunch` / `fx.kick` | 4821, 4822 | **no-ops by owner order — not findings** |

**Count: 9 channels on an ordinary bite, 11 on a building, 12 on a landmark.** That is a genuinely thick event and absence #1 is closed on the bite. The problems are in *when* and *what for whom* — below.

## PART 2 — FINDINGS

### The hit-stop freezes the world 130 ms before the mouth opens
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:4820 and src/proto3d/void3d.ts:1930-1937

EVIDENCE — the freeze is armed at 4820, the mouth is not started until 4917, 97 lines later in the same call:
```
4820:      hitStop(0.055 + 0.05 * bite);
4917:  voidling.chomp(bite);   // graded by how big that was relative to us
```
The hero animates on frozen time (`prototype3d.ts:8553`):
```
  voidling.update(dtw, { t: tClock, x: voidState.x, z: voidState.z, vx, vz,
```
and `dtw` is scaled to 6 % while the freeze runs (`prototype3d.ts:7986`):
```
  if (stopT > 0) { stopT = Math.max(0, stopT - dt); dtw *= 0.06; }
```
The envelope it is freezing (`void3d.ts:1930-1937`):
```
      if (mouthT > 0) { mouthT -= dt; mouthAge += dt; }
      let openEnv = 1;
      if (mouthAge < 0.045) openEnv = (mouthAge / 0.045) * 0.12;
      else {
        const t2 = mouthAge - 0.045;
        openEnv = 1 - 0.88 * Math.exp(-t2 * 10) * Math.cos(t2 * 14);
      }
```
Arithmetic: a landmark bite (`bite > 0.55`) freezes for 82–105 ms. At 6 % that advances `mouthAge` by **5–6 ms**, so `openEnv` reaches **0.013** — the jaw is 1.3 % open for the entire freeze. The 111 % overshoot peak is at `mouthAge = 0.22`, i.e. **~130 ms after the freeze has already ended.**

WHY: on the one moment the game stops time to say "that was big", the void's mouth is shut and nothing is moving. The child feels a hitch attached to no picture — which is exactly the "motion bump once in a while" complaint that the shake round chased. Hit-stop's whole job is to hold the peak frame; here it holds the frame before frame one.

FIX: move `hitStop(...)` from 4820 to immediately after `voidling.chomp(bite)` at 4917 and delay it by the wind-up — either arm it with a 45 ms lead-in, or set `mouthAge = 0.045` (skip the wind-up) on a landmark bite so the maw is springing open when the world stops. Smallest single change: relocate line 4820 below 4917 and change the wind-up test to `mouthAge < 0.045 && stopT <= 0`.

GATE: `qa/juice.mjs`. It currently counts four booleans (`juice.mjs:53-57`) and never looks at the mouth. Add `maw` to `__juiceState()` (`prototype3d.ts:1621`) and assert that on the forced bite the maw's scale exceeds 0.6 while `stop > 0`. Fails today (maw ≈ 0.26, the hungry-mood floor from `void3d.ts:1166`), passes after.

### Nothing the size of a building anticipates anything — lean, drift and the hungry face all die on the same guard
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:8715

EVIDENCE:
```
8715:    const inWell = d < reach && e.radius < 2.5 && (!e.mesh.userData.mover || e.radius < 0.9) && e.radius <= R * eatRatioNow();
```
Everything anticipatory lives inside `else if (inWell)`:
```
8741:      if (d < reach * 0.85) hungryT = tClock;   // food in the well: the face gets HUNGRY
8752:      const leanK = Math.min(0.75, (1 - d / reach) * 1.35);
8753:      e.mesh.rotation.z = (dx / d) * leanK;
8754:      e.mesh.rotation.x = -(dz / d) * leanK;
```
and the comment three lines above the lean states the intent it can never serve:
```
8747:      // The single frame this genre sells itself on is a lamppost or a hotel
8748:      // keeling over the rim and hanging there for a beat before it goes, and at
8749:      // nine degrees we were not taking that frame. 0.75 rad is 43 degrees
```
A hotel cannot reach that code: houses are registered at radius 2.0–8.0 (`src/proto3d/island.ts:5055` `plant('bathhouse', 22, 74, 4.6, NM.makeKura, false, 'house')`; `:5348` `plant('greek', 24, 140, 7.0, TG.makeFratHouse, true, 'house')`). Anything not edible yet gets contact-only acknowledgement — a 0.05 rad (2.9°) wobble on a fixed axis:
```
8731:      if (d < R + e.radius * 0.7 && !(e.mesh.userData.shakeT > 0)) e.mesh.userData.shakeT = 0.45;
8766:      e.mesh.rotation.z = ud.shakeT > 0 ? Math.sin(tClock * 42) * 0.05 * (ud.shakeT / 0.45) : 0;
```
So a house: stands perfectly still → is captured on one frame → topples and drains. And because `hungryT` is inside the same branch, **the void's own face never goes hungry approaching a landmark** (`prototype3d.ts:8514` `else if (tClock - hungryT < 0.45) mood = 'hungry';`).

WHY: the biggest, most-anticipated bite in the game is the only one with no wind-up on either side — absences #2 and #4 landing together on the money shot. Everything under r 2.5 leans and slides in beautifully; the bathhouse does not so much as tilt.

FIX: split the lean from the magnet. Compute `leanK` for any prop with `d < reach && e.radius <= R * eatRatioNow()` (drop only the `radius < 2.5` clause for the rotation and for `hungryT`), and keep the position drift gated as it is — "buildings stay founded" is the deliberate call, "buildings stay rigid" was not.

GATE: extend `qa/juice.mjs` (or a small `qa/anticipate.mjs`): warp to a house-sized prop with `__warpVoid` at `__setVoidR` big enough to eat it, step to `d ≈ 0.8 * reach`, and assert `|mesh.rotation.z| + |mesh.rotation.x| > 0.15` and `__voidState().mood === 'hungry'` **before** capture. Both are 0 / 'cruise' today.

### Backgrounding the app demotes the graphics rung; three interruptions latch shadows off for the session and cost a 1,677 ms freeze
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:9165

EVIDENCE — the accumulator takes **unclamped** wall time and nothing resets it when the page comes back:
```
9165:  qAccT += dtRaw; qAccN++; qCd -= dt;
9166:  if (qPinned === null && started && qCd <= 0 && qAccT > 0) {
9167:    const avg = qAccN / qAccT; qAccN = 0; qAccT = 0;
9168:    if (avg < 46 && qLevel < QUALITY.length - 1) { qLevel++; applyQuality(); qCd = 4; }
```
`dtRaw` is `clock.getDelta()` (`:7980`), unbounded. Backgrounding is an explicit, handled state — it pauses the match (`:6253-6257`) but `started` stays true and the ladder is not gated on `paused`:
```
6253:  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
6254:    if (document.hidden && started && !ended && !paused) {
6255:      paused = true; paintPause(); pauseEl.classList.add('show');
```
`rAF` stops while hidden, so the first frame back carries the whole gap. A 30-second phone call gives `avg = ~180 / ~33 = 5 fps` → guaranteed demote. `qAccT` is only zeroed *inside* the check, so a gap that lands mid-cooldown still poisons the next check. One demote per backgrounding; the rungs (`:970-977`) are pixel-ratio 2.0 → 1.6 → 1.35 (**bloom off**) → 1.15 (**shadows off**), and rung 3 is a one-way door:
```
1039:    renderer.shadowMap.enabled = wantShadows;
1041:    if (!wantShadows) qShadowLatch = true;
```
with the cost documented at `:1044-1046`: *"a 1,677 ms frame and 3,190 ms of extra work spread over the next 60 frames."*

WHY: this is a children's game on a shared iPad. Three interruptions in one session — a call banner, Control Centre, a switch to YouTube — and the child comes back to a 1.7-second freeze, then plays the rest of the session with no shadows and 33 % of the pixels, on hardware that was never struggling. It also flips the bloom pipeline mid-session, which is the owner's own repeated "colour keeps switching" report.

FIX: one line. `qAccT += Math.min(dtRaw, 0.5);` at 9165 — still catches the 200 ms hitches task #40 exists for, cannot be poisoned by a suspend. (Belt and braces: zero `qAccT`/`qAccN` and set `qCd = 3` in the `visibilitychange` handler when the page becomes visible.)

GATE: new `qa/bgquality.mjs`. Start a match, read `__quality().level` (hook exists at `:1750`), open a second Playwright page for 8 s so the first backgrounds, return, wait past `qCd`, re-read. Today the level increments; after the fix it does not. Repeat ×3 and assert `__quality().shadows` is still true.

with `evolveT = 0.7` set at `:1497`, and `uniformK` multiplying the whole body at `:1805-1806` (`squash *= uniformK; bob.scale.set(dispR * lat, dispR * squash, dispR * lat)`). Evaluated:

### The intro does not disable the controls — it taxes them 31 %, and the comment says 99.8 %
SEVERITY: polish
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:8100

EVIDENCE:
```
8100:    if (introT > 0) { const dk = Math.pow(0.9, dt * 60); velX *= dk; velZ *= dk; }
```
This runs 233 lines *before* the velocity is recomputed from the stick (`:8333`):
```
    velX += (tvx - velX) * k;
```
so the damping is applied to last frame's velocity and immediately re-accelerated in the same frame. With `k = dt * 11 = 0.183` at 60 fps, the fixed point is `v = 0.183 / (1 − 0.9·0.817) · tvx` = **0.69 · tvx**. The comment that describes this (`:5198`) claims otherwise:
```
  // fired here, in the same block that sets introT = 2.2 — and the intro damps
  // velocity by 0.9^(dt*60) for those 2.2 seconds, roughly 0.0018x per second.
```

WHY: not a bug you can see so much as a wrong belief in the file — but it means that for the whole establishing shot, with the camera 300 units up and diving, a child who drags gets a real but sluggish response and no instruction (`showGuide` only fires at `introT <= 0`, `:8812-8823`). That is the first 90 seconds, absence #6's flagship seam. Either commit to 100 % control during the intro or to 0 %; 69 % with the camera elsewhere is the one option that reads as broken.

FIX: move line 8100 to immediately after 8333, or delete it and let the intro's own camera do the work. Correct the comment at 5198 either way.

GATE: `qa/_startlag.mjs` (already measures tap→score across starts). Add: hold full stick from t=0 and record displacement during `introT > 0` — assert it is either < 5 % or > 95 % of settled-play displacement for the same input, not 69 %.

## PART 4 — THE WORLD KNOWS YOU ARE THERE: honest answer

**People: yes, and well.** `src/proto3d/life.ts:2566`:
```
        } else if (dist < vR + fear && calmT <= 0) {
```
with `fear` documented at `:2050-2051` as *"fear is 18-20 units against a 0.9-unit void"* — so a wanderer reacts at roughly 19 units of clearance, never on contact. The three-act Lantern behaviour (`:2546-2565`) adds a *greet* band at `vR + fear * 2.4` (~46 u) and a *freeze-and-stare* band at `vR + fear * 1.6` (~31 u), and the panic contagion at `:2607-2612` propagates a scream 25 units to neighbours. Set pieces carry their own bands: `:3340` `vR + 20`, `:3192` `vR + 34`, `:4229` `vR + 40`, `:5520` `d < vR + 55`. The crowd genuinely anticipates.

**Props: partially, and the gap is the finding above.** Anything under radius 2.5 drifts and leans from `reach = R * 2.0 + e.radius * 2.4` (`:8714`) — real proximity anticipation, and at up to 43° it is the best single frame in the build. Anything at or above 2.5 — every house, every landmark, every hero prop — has **no proximity channel at all**, and neither does the hero's face when approaching one.

**Nothing else in the world anticipates.** No light, sign, flag, awning or window changes state on the void's approach; the only non-crowd reaction anywhere is the 2.9° contact wobble at `:8766`.

---

## PART 5 — INPUT: honest answer, no findings

I looked for problems here and did not find any I would defend.

- **Deadzone**: 10 px. `:8226` `if (joy.active && joy.mag > 0.156)` against `JOY_R = 64` (`:2657`); the speed ramp uses the same floor (`:8271` `THREE.MathUtils.clamp((joy.mag - 0.156) / (0.58 - 0.156), 0, 1)`), so full throttle is at 37 px, not the rim — the measured cure for the "keep dragging" complaint.
- **Heading**: smoothed, amplitude-weighted, never snapped (`:2723-2731`): `const w = 0.28 + 0.72 * joy.mag * joy.mag;` then renormalised to a unit vector. Direction and magnitude are separated so the ramp cannot be squared, which is a bug this file has already had and fixed.
- **Edge**: `JOY_EDGE = 22`, base slides away from a bezel at `JOY_STEP = 16 px/tick` (`:2701-2708`), gated on `joy.moved` so a tap never flings, and driven off the frame loop as well as off events (`:2783` `function joyEdgeTick(): void { if (joyPinned()) joySet(joy.px, joy.py); }`) because a pinned thumb stops emitting `pointermove`. `qa/joyedge.mjs` is the gate and it is real.
- **Release**: four paths, all routed through one function (`:2803-2806`) — `pointerup`/`pointercancel`, `blur`, `visibilitychange`, plus explicit calls at `resetMatch` (`:6099`) and pause-open (`:6265`). Two-finger ownership is provisional until one has driven (`:2748` `if (joy.active && joy.moved) return;`).
- **Coast on release**: `k = min(1, dt * 4.5)` (`:8332`) ≈ 222 ms — deliberate and consistent with the ice model.

The only thing I would even mention: `joyEl.style.display` flips instantly on both press and release (`:2759`, `:2805`) while the void coasts for ~222 ms afterwards, so the stick vanishes before the motion does. Sub-polish; not worth a change.

---

## HONEST EMPTIES

- **Anticipation and settle on the ordinary bite is done and correct.** Mouth: three-phase, 45 ms wind-up → spring → 11.8 % overshoot at 220 ms → settled by 400 ms (`void3d.ts:1930-1937`, computed above). Scale: an underdamped spring at 95/9.0 with a direct `impulse()` shove, not a lerp (`void3d.ts:1732-1736`). Retrigger cannot shrink the maw (`:1703-1709`). Direction-flip anticipation exists (`:1761-1763`). Mood params lerp at `dt * 9` (`:1947`), never snap. This front was genuinely closed; my findings are at its edges, not its centre.
- **Particle fade is done** (`:8776` `const f = Math.min(1, puffLife[i] / 0.18);`) — no spark blinks out at brightness.
- **Look-ahead scaling is done** (`:8880` `const leadScale = Math.max(1, camDist / 60);`).
- **Camera shake / kick / lens punch**: verified dead at source (`fx.ts:118` `shake(amt) { void amt; }`, `:120-126` `kick(...) { void dx; void dz; void amt; }`, `prototype3d.ts:551` `const camPunch = (deg: number) => { void deg; };`). Owner's order. Not findings, not counted, not proposed.
- I found nothing wrong with the audio grading of a bite, the combo pentatonic ladder, the drain-spiral mass scaling, the containment/coast handling, or the joystick. Those are all better than the category.

COVERAGE: docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/AAA-BRIEF.md (§0–§4.4, §7 ledger in full), qa/README.md, qa/juice.mjs, qa/uisystem.mjs, src/prototype3d.ts (lines 355–400, 535–560, 950–1060, 2300–2430, 2480–2500, 2600–2860, 2960–3000, 4494–4545, 4680–4700, 4765–5060, 5160–5200, 5270–5440, 5575–5620, 6090–6320, 7955–8000, 8090–8150, 8215–8400, 8500–8560, 8640–8790, 8790–8980, 9140–9228), src/proto3d/void3d.ts (1440–1510, 1685–1760, 1756–1812, 1920–1975), src/proto3d/fx.ts (whole file), src/proto3d/life.ts (2040–2075, 2499–2640, proximity-threshold census), src/proto3d/audio3d.ts (3983–4092), src/proto3d/bubbles.ts (100–180, 274–305), src/proto3d/island.ts (4968–5361, house radii), index.html (69, 186–240, 340–430, 555–630, 674–706, 743–840, 855–915, 985–1100, 1154–1180, 1249–1300, 1355–1370, 1425–1500, 1580–1600, 1820–1830, 1921).

### The iOS home-screen label still says VOIDLING
SEVERITY: blocker
AT: ios/App/App/Info.plist:9
EVIDENCE:
```
	<key>CFBundleDisplayName</key>
        <string>VOIDLING</string>
```
and capacitor.config.ts:9 —
```
  appName: 'World Ender',
```
`grep -rn "DisplayName\|World Ender" ios/App/App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj ios/App/App/*.plist` returns only these; no `INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName` anywhere in the pbxproj (`PRODUCT_NAME = "$(TARGET_NAME)"` at :309 and :330).
WHY: `npx cap sync ios` copies `webDir` and `capacitor.config.json`; it does not rewrite `Info.plist`. `appName` is consumed at `cap add`/scaffold time and by Android's `strings.xml` — it has never written iOS's `CFBundleDisplayName`. So the icon on the child's home screen reads **VOIDLING** while the App Store listing reads *The Cute World Ender*. HANDOFF.md:28 asserts the opposite mechanism as settled fact ("Home-screen label | **World Ender** | 11 chars — fits untruncated. Set via `capacitor.config.ts` `appName`"), so the one artifact that would have caught this is the artifact that says it is already handled. This is also the exact name the rename existed to escape (HANDOFF.md:32 — "Voidling" is a live App Store arcade game). A reviewer installs the build, looks at the springboard, and sees a different app name from the one on the listing.
FIX: one string — `Info.plist:10` → `<string>World Ender</string>`. (Also worth checking `CFBundleDisplayName` is what `store/*.png` device-frame shots show.)
GATE: none exists. The smallest one: extend `qa/iapdoc.mjs` — which already exists to catch `APPSTORE.md` drifting from the client — with a native-metadata section asserting `Info.plist` `CFBundleDisplayName` equals the documented home-screen label in `docs/HANDOFF.md`. It fails on HEAD.

### The iOS status bar is drawn over the game — two clocks, and the HUD is designed around it
SEVERITY: major
AT: ios/App/App/Info.plist:39
EVIDENCE:
```
	<key>UIStatusBarHidden</key>
	<true/>
...
	<key>UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance</key>
	<true/>
```
against capacitor.config.ts:15 —
```
    StatusBar: {
      style: 'DARK',
      backgroundColor: '#14082B',
      overlaysWebView: true,
    },
```
and `@capacitor/status-bar: ^8.0.2` is a real dependency (package.json:89), so the plugin config is live, not inert.
WHY: `UIStatusBarHidden` only controls the bar *during launch*. With `UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance` true, the root view controller wins the moment the UI appears — and Capacitor's bridge controller reports the bar visible by default, with `overlaysWebView: true` explicitly asking it to sit *on top of* the web view. Net: the child plays with the iOS clock, carrier and battery painted over the sky for all three minutes, directly above a match timer that is itself a clock. Two clocks, one band. That is the owner's phone photo. The CSS is written correctly for this case — `index.html:120` `top: max(12px, calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)))` puts `#timer` 12px below the safe area, i.e. 71px down on an iPhone 15 Pro — but 12px is the *whole* clearance under the Dynamic Island for a 31px numeral. Every polished title in this genre hides the bar outright.
FIX: decide, in one place. If the bar should be gone: `UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance` → `<false/>` (so `UIStatusBarHidden` is honoured), and drop the `StatusBar` block from `capacitor.config.ts`. If it stays, raise the top-band offsets from `+12px` to `+20px` so the clock is not shouldered against the Island.
GATE: this one cannot be probed from Chromium — it is native. It belongs on the device checklist for HANDOFF §8 step 4 ("First build to his iPhone via cable"), as a named line: *photograph the top 100px of a match and confirm what is in it.*

### The final-ten countdown is the least legible element in the game, and it is worst on the newest world
SEVERITY: major
AT: index.html:392
EVIDENCE:
```
      #count span { font-size: min(30vw, 150px); font-weight: 700; color: #ffd23f;
        text-shadow: 0 5px 0 rgba(60,20,10,0.5), 0 0 38px rgba(255,180,60,0.55);
        opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.6); }
```
The ground it lands on, src/proto3d/island.ts:757 —
```
    // 1. BASE — dusk snow: pale blue-white, never pure white
    g.fillStyle = '#dfe7f6'; g.fillRect(0, 0, TEX, TEX);
```
WHY: `0 5px 0` is a hard *offset* drop, not an outline — it darkens the bottom edge of the glyph and nothing else; `0 0 38px` is a soft Gaussian bloom, which lightens the surround. So the numeral has no outline at all. Gold `#ffd23f` (rel. luminance 0.687) against Powder Pass's snow bake `#dfe7f6` (0.787) is **1.14:1** — below even the 3:1 large-text floor, by a factor of three. The `.hot` variant `#ff6a5e` at ≤3s is better but still ~2.4:1 on snow. This is a 150px numeral at the single most dramatic moment of the match, on the world a child reaches last, and it fires on every single run. The file's own comment two hundred lines down already diagnosed this exact class of miss for `#evolve` (index.html:545: *"#timer, #titlecard and #banner were each measured against the live world and given a hard treatment… #evolve was skipped"*) — the fix was applied to `#evolve` and `#count` was left behind.
FIX: give it `#timer`'s idiom, which works on any ground and needs no markup — `-webkit-text-stroke: 5px rgba(12,6,26,0.92); paint-order: stroke fill;` on `#count span` (5px rather than 3px because the glyph is 4× the size).
GATE: `qa/contrast2.mjs`. It measures the right thing the right way (chrome-against-its-own-backing, so an outline is visible to it) but its ID list is `qa/contrast2.mjs:34` `const IDS = ['board','timer','coins','btnQuit','growth']` and its default world list is `'lantern,maple,gameday'` — it has never looked at `#count`, and has never looked at Powder. Add `count`/`evolve`/`banner` to `IDS`, add `powder` to the default worlds, drive `__rushClock` so the countdown is on screen, and give the probe an exit code (it currently prints and exits 0, so `qa/gate.mjs` could not use it even if it were listed).

plus `#banner .bCard` (`408: backdrop-filter: blur(9px);`) on every beat, and `#end` on the results screen —
```
678:      #end { position: fixed; inset: 0; … background: rgba(13,8,33,0.82); backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
```
`grep -c backdrop-filter index.html` = **18 declarations total**.
WHY: each one forces its own compositing layer that must sample the canvas's freshly-rendered output every frame. `#growth` alone is `min(92vw, 460px)` wide — a ~460×45 blur strip re-read at 60Hz — and the panels behind them are already `0.88` and `0.91-0.93` opaque, so the blur is buying almost nothing visually (the file's own comment at index.html:158 says the opacity change is what fixed the contrast; the blur is described only as what "keeps it from reading as a solid box"). `#end` is the worst single case: a **full-screen** backdrop blur held up for as long as a child reads their results, over a scene that is still rendering (see next finding). On a tier-C device this is the difference between the 30fps floor in the AAA-BRIEF §7 budget and a thermal throttle. It is listed in HANDOFF §9 as an open Phase-2 item, so this is a measurement, not a re-litigation.
FIX: delete `backdrop-filter` from the five match-time selectors and raise the panel fills the ~0.04 that costs (`0.88 → 0.92`). Replace `#end`'s blur with a solid `--panel-deep` scrim; the results card is opaque chrome, it does not need to show the town through itself.
GATE: `qa/qualcost.mjs` exists and is not in the release gate. Extend it to count `getComputedStyle(el).backdropFilter !== 'none'` over all visible elements during a live match and fail above N (N=0 for match-time chrome). Static and cheap — no frame timing required, so the swiftshader trap does not apply.

### The 3D scene renders at full rate behind every opaque full-screen overlay, including the pause sheet
SEVERITY: major
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:9202
EVIDENCE: the tail of `animate()` —
```
  if (bloomOn) {
    const c = ensureComposer();
    c.setPixelRatio(renderer.getPixelRatio());
    c.setSize(renderer.domElement.clientWidth, renderer.domElement.clientHeight);
    c.render();
  } else {
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(animate);
```
There is no guard. The only `visibilitychange` handlers are prototype3d.ts:2813 (`joyRelease`) and :6254 (raise the pause sheet) — neither touches rendering. `paused` gates only the simulation block at :7992 (`if (started && !ended && !paused)`); the render call is outside it.
The overlays that are fully opaque and cover `inset: 0`:
```
855:      #menu { position: fixed; inset: 0; … background: radial-gradient(…, #33175e 0%, #1c0f3d 46%, #0d0821 100%); }
624:      #book { position: fixed; inset: 0; … background: #150f24;
1323:      .metaScr { position: fixed; inset: 0; … background: #0d0821;      /* worlds, trophies, top voids */
1361:        background: rgba(13,8,33,0.94); backdrop-filter: blur(8px);      /* #shop */
1453:      #policy { position: fixed; inset: 0; … background: #14082a; }
1154:      #loadScr { position: fixed; inset: 0; …                            /* opaque gradient */
```
WHY: a child idling on the menu, browsing the scrapbook, reading the world picker, or **paused for dinner** is running a full three-minute-match render loop — shadow map updates every other frame (prototype3d.ts:9201 `if ((shadowFrame++ & 1) === 0) renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true;`) — behind a picture they cannot see through. On the pause sheet it is worse than pointless: the sim is frozen, so it re-renders an identical frame 60 times a second under a `blur(6px)` full-screen backdrop. The concrete symptom on the owner's phone is heat and battery, and on a hand-me-down iPad it is the app being killed. Also a listed Phase-2 item (HANDOFF §9), reported here with the exact call site.
FIX: one early-out at the top of the render tail — if `paused` or `document.body.classList.contains('menu')` or any of the opaque overlay ids carries `.show`, render at most every 4th frame (or skip entirely while `paused`, since nothing moves). Keep `requestAnimationFrame` running so the HUD's CSS animations and the cover release still tick.
GATE: `qa/qualcost.mjs` again, or a small new probe: stub `renderer.render` with a counter, open the pause sheet, sample the counter over 2s of `__matchState().t`-independent wall time, and assert it stops climbing. It will fail on HEAD.

### The world picker's SOLO toggle sits inside the home-indicator inset
SEVERITY: minor
AT: index.html:1263
EVIDENCE:
```
      #soloTog { position: absolute; right: 18px; bottom: 18px; z-index: 3; cursor: pointer;
        display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px;
        background: rgba(28,12,52,0.82); border: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16); border-radius: 14px;
        color: #cbb2ff; font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.4px;
        padding: 9px 16px; }
```
Its containing block, index.html:1323 —
```
      .metaScr { position: fixed; inset: 0; … 
        padding-top: calc(env(safe-area-inset-top) + 26px);
        padding-bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 12px); overflow-y: auto; }
```
WHY: an absolutely-positioned child resolves `bottom` against its containing block's **padding box**, which for a `position: fixed; inset: 0` parent is the whole viewport — the parent's `padding-bottom` does not push it up. So `bottom: 18px` is 18px from the physical bottom of the screen, inside the 34pt home-indicator inset that the same rule set five lines above is careful to reserve for everything else. The white indicator pill draws across the toggle's lower edge, and it is in the band iOS reserves for the swipe-up gesture. `#soloTog` is the only element in the file that anchors to the bottom without `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` and is actually visible (`#hunger`/`#hungerlbl`/`#powers` at :527 are `display: none !important`). Note the comment at :1319 documenting this exact class of miss being fixed for `.metaScr`'s top: *"SAFE AREA. This was a bare 26px while every other element in the file uses env(safe-area-inset-top)… An omission, not a decision."* Same omission, opposite edge, same screen.
FIX: `bottom: calc(18px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); right: calc(18px + env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px));`
GATE: no probe simulates insets except `qa/endlayout.mjs`, and it does so with two hard-coded selectors (`qa/endlayout.mjs:46-48`: `#end { padding-top: calc(54px + 59px) !important; } .endGo { padding-bottom: calc(10px + 34px) !important; }`). Replace that hack with a general injection — `:root { --sa-top: 59px; --sa-bottom: 34px; }` plus an `env()`→`var()` shim — and reuse it in `qa/hudsize.mjs`, asserting that no visible interactive element's rect intrudes into the bottom 34px or the top 59px. It fails on HEAD for `#soloTog`.

## Honest empties

- **Safe areas, top edge.** Every fixed element in the top band uses `env(safe-area-inset-top)` correctly — `#timer` (:120), `#board` (:150), `#coins` (:465), `#btnQuit` (:978), `#news` (:331), `#end` (:698), `#book` (:626), `#menu` (:857), `.metaScr` (:1325), `#shop` (:1362), `#btnSettings` (:1279), `.polBar` (:1456). `viewport-fit=cover` is present (:5). The only bottom-edge miss that is actually visible is `#soloTog`. I looked for others and there are none — `#hunger`, `#hungerlbl` and `#powers` are `display: none !important` at :527.
- **HUD contrast.** Aside from `#count` and `.vf`, every readout over the playfield has a real treatment and the reasoning for each is written next to it: `#timer` and `#evolve` carry 3px/2.5px strokes with `paint-order`, `#board`/`#coins`/`#btnQuit` sit on 0.88 panels with a measurement of *why* 0.88, `#titlecard` has a radial scrim, `#news`/`#guide`/`#banner .bCard` are solid cards. This area has been worked hard and it shows.
- **Results-screen layout.** `#end` is genuinely well solved — the flex-start + auto-margin scroll (:672-699), the sticky `.endGo` with a solid fill and a gradient apron above it (:711-722), the reserved top strip for the coin chip, and `qa/endlayout.mjs` gating it at three sizes with simulated insets. I found nothing to add.
- **Reduced motion.** A real `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block exists (:1651) and it thinks about the specific cases (the shop sparkles that would otherwise pile up, the growth bar's sheen). Better than most shipping games.
- **Landscape / iPad clipping.** The app is portrait-locked in `Info.plist:35-38` and `:43-46` and `manifest.json` (`"orientation": "portrait"`), so `.metaScr`'s missing horizontal insets cannot bite. Not a finding.

COVERAGE: docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/AAA-BRIEF.md, qa/README.md, index.html (lines 1–560, 560–1000, 1125–1340, 1400–1600, 1655–1900, plus full-file greps for `safe-area`, `backdrop-filter`, `box-sizing`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `cubic-bezier`, `position: fixed|absolute`, `@media`, `width: Npx`), src/prototype3d.ts (lines 636–760, 1775–1810, 5815–5880, 7965–8030, 8112–8140, 9160–9228, plus greps for render loop, visibilitychange, `✦`, cssText, shopGrid), src/proto3d/bubbles.ts (lines 1–180), src/proto3d/island.ts (lines 750–790), src/proto3d/palette.ts (grep), capacitor.config.ts, ios/App/App/Info.plist, ios/App/App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (grep), package.json, public/manifest.json, node_modules/@fontsource/fredoka/700.css, qa/gate.mjs, qa/uisystem.mjs, qa/contrast2.mjs, qa/hudsize.mjs, qa/endlayout.mjs, qa/endfit.mjs, qa/navfit.mjs, qa/hud3.mjs, qa/funnel.mjs, qa/portrait.mjs.

### The daily quest board hands two of five worlds a chip that cannot be cleared
SEVERITY: blocker
AT: src/prototype3d.ts:3187 and src/prototype3d.ts:3256

EVIDENCE:
```ts
const MED_Q = pickedWorld === 'pirate' ? ['evolve', 'combo', 'gold']
  : pickedWorld === 'powder' ? ['evolve', 'combo', 'gold'] : ['cars', 'evolve', 'combo'];
const HARD_Q = pickedWorld === 'pirate' ? ['cabanas', 'rival', 'big']
  : pickedWorld === 'powder' ? ['houses', 'rival', 'big'] : ['houses', 'rival', 'big'];
```
and the encore draw, which already knows this class of bug exists but names one world:
```ts
  const banned = new Set(['gulp', 'collapse', 'solo',
    ...(pickedWorld === 'pirate' ? ['cars', 'houses'] : ['cabanas'])]);
```
with its own comment two lines above (src/prototype3d.ts:3253): `// impossible quests are excluded (POWERS_ON is false; pirate has no cars or // houses; cabanas exist nowhere else).`

Credit only ever comes from a tag (src/prototype3d.ts:4978-4984): `if (e.radius >= 6) questEvent('big'); … if (qk) questEvent(qk); … if (qk === 'rv') questEvent('house');`

The tags do not exist on those two worlds:
- **LANTERN NIGHT has no car.** Every `qk = 'car'` assignment in the repo is Maple (src/proto3d/island.ts:6219,6224,6225; src/proto3d/life.ts:2407,4551, both inside `worldId() === 'maple'` guards) or Pirate's shuttle buggies (src/proto3d/life.ts:3151). The Lantern populate block (src/proto3d/island.ts:4939-5228) tags only `'house'` and `'big'`.
- **POWDER PASS has no house.** Its block tags `'lodge'`, `'chalet'`, `'snowman'`, `'pine'`, `'drift'`, `'lift'`, `'sign'`, `'hut'`, `'snowballs'` — src/proto3d/island.ts:4797-4846. Grepping every `'house'` tag in the build returns only Lantern's stalls and Game Day's frat/brick halls (src/proto3d/island.ts:5015-5172, 5395, 5408) plus the GLB name rule at src/proto3d/assets3d.ts:121.
- **POWDER PASS also has only one landmark.** `'big'` needs three objects at `radius >= 6`; the only one in Powder is the Lodge — `drop(lodge, [PW.LODGE.cx, PW.LODGE.cy], 10.5, …, 'lodge')` (src/proto3d/island.ts:4797). Everything else in that block tops out at 4.4 (the bell tower). Lantern by contrast has five `'big'` drops (island.ts:4983,4984,4985,5000,5007) so its hard slot is fine.

Replaying the shipped draw (`daySeed` hash + the disjoint `draw()` at src/prototype3d.ts:3213-3222) over 365 days:

| world | days/365 the board carries an unclearable chip |
|---|---|
| maple / pirate / gameday | 0 |
| **lantern** | **149** (`cars`) |
| **powder** | **234** (`houses` 128 + `big` 106) — only `rival` is ever clearable in the hard slot |

WHY: the quest board is the game's primary come-back-tomorrow hook and it is on screen in every match (`#quests`) and on every results card (`endQuests`, src/prototype3d.ts:4657). On Lantern Night, two days in five, a six-year-old spends three minutes at a night market being told 🚗 0/6. On Powder Pass — the newest world, the one a child reaches last and is meant to stay for — the hard chip is dead on 64% of days. Because `questComplete()` only fires the +25✦ board bonus and the encore chip when `quests.every(x => x.done)` (src/prototype3d.ts:3275-3278), one dead chip also kills the clear bonus **and** the encore loop that exists so the board never says "come back tomorrow" mid-sitting. The rest of the day's play pays nothing extra no matter how well they do.

FIX: two lines. Give Lantern its own MED list (`['evolve','combo','gold']`, same as pirate/powder) and give Powder a hard list without `houses` or `big` (`['rival','snack','gild']`, or tag its chalets `'house'` — a chalet *is* a house and that also lights up FIRST BUILDING and the newsroom's house headlines, which are equally dead there today). Then extend the `banned` set to be a per-world table rather than `pirate ? … : …`.

GATE: new `qa/questfit.mjs` — for each of the five worlds, read `window.__edibles` after the world settles and assert every id reachable from `EASY_Q ∪ MED_Q ∪ HARD_Q ∪ (QUEST_POOL − banned)` has at least `target` objects that can satisfy it. It fails on lantern and powder on today's build. (`qa/econ.mjs` is the natural home for the +25✦ board-clear half of the assertion.)

SEVERITY: major
AT: src/game/stickers.ts:242 (the POWDER set) and src/prototype3d.ts:5768

### A hunter bite demotes you, the score floor refunds it the next frame, and the game plays the EVOLVE fanfare for it
SEVERITY: **blocker**
AT: `src/prototype3d.ts:2352` · `src/prototype3d.ts:8203` · `src/prototype3d.ts:8217` · `src/prototype3d.ts:8934`

EVIDENCE:

```
2351:    const st = stageFor(voidling.radius);
2352:    const down = Math.max(START_R, (FORM_MIN[Math.max(0, st - 1)] || START_R) * 1.02);
2353:    voidling.setRadius(Math.max(START_R, Math.min(voidling.radius * hit.shrink, down)));
2354:    if (st > 0) {
2355:      curStage = stageFor(voidling.radius);
```
```
8203:      if (!frozenR && voidling.radius > lastR + maxStep) voidling.setRadius(lastR + maxStep);
8204:      if (!frozenR && voidling.radius > lawCap) voidling.setRadius(lawCap);
8205:      lastR = voidling.radius;
...
8217:      const scoreFloor = Math.min(lawCap, START_R * (1 + Math.pow(playerScore / 974, 0.57)) + surgeT * surgeT * 2.6 * pace);
8218:      if (!frozenR && voidling.radius < scoreFloor) voidling.setRadius(scoreFloor);
```
```
8933:  const ns = stageFor(voidling.radius);
8934:  if (ns > curStage) {
8935:    curStage = ns;
```

WHY: Three facts compose into one bug, all on the same frame budget.

1. `down` is *always* one rung below the current one, for every rung. `0.85·FORM_MIN[st] > 1.02·FORM_MIN[st-1]` holds at every st (1.36>0.918, 2.125>1.632, 3.06>2.55, 4.675>3.672, 6.8>5.61), so a connecting hunter bite lands the void exactly on `down` and `curStage` drops by one, every time.
2. The score floor at :8218 is applied **after** `lastR` is written at :8205, so `maxStep` cannot rate-limit it. The restore is a single-frame jump, not a climb.
3. The bite only takes 8 % of score (`rivals.ts:1311` `Math.min(1200, Math.round(pScore * 0.08))`), which moves `START_R*(1+pow(S/974,0.57))` by 4.7 %. The player was pinned at `lawCap` before the bite (the floor exceeds `lawCap` from roughly half-par onward), so 4.7 % is not enough to un-pin them.

Worked through at t=30 s, par score 3240, radius pinned at `lawCap` = 2.31: steal = 259 → S = 2981 → next frame `lawCap` = 2.265, raw floor = 2.603 → `scoreFloor` = 2.265. Net permanent cost of being caught: **0.045 units, 1.9 %**. And because `curStage` was walked back to 0 while `stageFor(2.265)` is 1, line 8934 fires the **entire evolution ceremony**: the EVOLVED card with the form name, `audio.evolve()`, `camPunch(5)`, `camDist *= 1.07`, `fx.ring`, `buzz(45)`, `holdBanner(2.4)`, `track('evolve')`, and from GOBBLIN up `townReacts({kind:'evolve'})` — the newsroom prints a headline congratulating the void on growing, one second after it was eaten.

What the child sees: red flash → "BONK!! back to VOIDLING!! 💫" → the body barely moves (`void3d.ts:1728` only snaps `dispR` past `max(1.5, r*0.5)`, and the drop is smaller than that) → "EVOLVED! MUNCHKIN" with the full fanfare. The game's single biggest punishment is delivered as a reward, several times per match, on the one character the banner promises "CHASES you". The comment at `prototype3d.ts:2338` claims this was fixed — *"Shrink alone can be refunded by the growth law; points cannot"* — and the arithmetic above says it was not.

FIX: Two lines. Move `lastR = voidling.radius;` from :8205 to after the score-floor clamp at :8218, so the floor is rate-limited like everything else; and give the evolve block a high-water mark (`let bestStage = 0;` reset in `resetMatch`, `if (ns > curStage) { curStage = ns; if (ns > bestStage) { bestStage = ns; …ceremony… } }`) so a form already earned this match never re-announces. The demotion HUD/float at :2379 keeps working; only the fanfare is suppressed.

GATE: `qa/_rf_evorefire.mjs <world>` already exists and already prints `RE-FIRES: n` — it is the negative control for exactly this claim and appears never to have been run to a verdict (no ledger entry, no retraction). It fails before (`RE-FIRES > 0`) and passes after (`RE-FIRES == 0`). Promote it out of the `_` throwaway pool. `qa/newsarc.mjs` should also stop seeing an `evolve` reaction inside 2 s of a `caught` event.

### Pirate Bay's leftover treasure chests replay their swallow animation — and puff dust around the void — at the start of every rematch
SEVERITY: major
AT: `src/prototype3d.ts:6085` · `src/prototype3d.ts:6149` · `src/prototype3d.ts:8671`

EVIDENCE:

```
6082: function clearBeatLoot() {
6083:   for (const e of beatLoot) {
6084:     if (!e.eaten && e.mesh.visible) spawnPuff(e.mesh.position.x, 0.6, e.mesh.position.z, 6);
6085:     e.eaten = true; e.mesh.visible = false;
6086:     // retired, or the rematch restore loop resurrects every leftover chest
6087:     e.mesh.userData.retired = true;
6088:     scene.remove(e.mesh);
6089:   }
6090:   beatLoot = [];
6091: }
```
```
6149:    if (e.mesh.userData.retired) { e.mesh.visible = false; if (e.mesh.parent) scene.remove(e.mesh); continue; }
6150:    e.eaten = false; e.t = 0;
```
```
8671:    if (e.eaten) {
...
8705:      if (e.t >= 1) {
8706:        // the puff marks where the THING went, not where the void is standing
8707:        spawnPuff(p.x, Math.max(0.2, cy * 0.4), p.z, 6);
8708:        scene.remove(e.mesh); e.eaten = false;
```

WHY: `clearBeatLoot()` sets `e.eaten = true` and marks the chest `retired`, but never removes it from `edibles`. `resetMatch`'s restore loop hits the `retired` guard at :6149 and `continue`s **before** the `e.eaten = false` on the next line — so 12 chests enter the new match still flagged eaten. The per-frame loop at :8671 tests `e.eaten` first, so all twelve run the full swallow spiral on a mesh that is invisible and no longer in the scene: their positions are rewritten to orbit `voidState` (`p.x = voidState.x + Math.cos(e.orbit) * r`), and at `e.t >= 1` each one calls `spawnPuff` at that position. The result is ~72 dust particles erupting around the void in the first half-second of every Pirate Bay PLAY AGAIN, from nothing. `spawnBeatTreasure` fires on Pirate's finale beat every single match (`at: 148`, clamped to ≤146 by the jitter block, `dur: 32` → the window closes at 174–178 s, so `clearBeatLoot` always runs before the whistle). PLAY AGAIN is how children actually start matches, so this is on the second-most-walked path in the game.

Secondary, same root: `edibles` grows by 12 entries per Pirate match for the life of the page — `spawnBeatTreasure` pushes (`:6077 beatLoot.push(edibles[edibles.length - 1]);`) and nothing ever splices. Maple's train has the same shape at `life.ts:4293` (`trainGrp.userData.retired = true; trainGrp = null; buildTrain();`) — every rebuild leaks a four-loco group with its geometries and materials undisposed.

FIX: one word — `clearBeatLoot` should leave the chest in the state a finished swallow leaves it: change `:6085` to `e.eaten = false; e.t = 1; e.mesh.visible = false;`. Better still, splice retired entries out of `edibles` in the `:6149` guard (`edibles.splice(i,1)` on an indexed loop) and dispose the meshes, which closes the leak at the same time.

GATE: `qa/rematch.mjs` — it already owns this exact class ("the two bugs that only exist on the second match"). Add: run a Pirate match to the whistle, PLAY AGAIN, and on the first frame of match 2 assert `__edibles.filter(e => e.eaten).length === 0` and that the puff count does not rise in the first second. Fails before, passes after.

Honest limit: I could not measure how many props each world actually retires — the `console.info` at :6008 reports it and nothing in the repo has recorded a run. If the count is zero on all five worlds the finding is inert; if it is non-zero the ceiling is off by exactly that fraction. The code is wrong either way (a denominator that can only grow, against a numerator that can shrink).

FIX: decrement in the cull loop — `if (cull[k] < initialMass) initialMass--;` beside the splice at :5954, or simpler, recompute `initialMass = edibles.length` at the tail of `validateWorld()` when `!started`.

GATE: `qa/val.mjs` already runs `__validateWorld()` on every world and reports the sweep line. Extend it to assert `initialMass === __edibles.length` after the sweep, and add a `devouredPct === 100` check to `qa/econ.mjs`'s solo path with every prop force-eaten.

### `formProgress` measures the first rung from a radius the void never has
SEVERITY: polish
AT: `src/prototype3d.ts:4095`

EVIDENCE:

```
4091:  // Every rung now measures from the largest of its threshold and the size a
4092:  // void actually starts at (spawn r=1.0 — START_R 0.9 is the SHRINK floor,
4093:  // below the start line): the bar begins EMPTY, as a bar should, and a void
4094:  // shrunk under 1.0 shows an honest 0%.
4095:  const lo = Math.max(FORM_MIN[st], 1), hi = FORM_MIN[st + 1] ?? R_CAP;
4096:  return THREE.MathUtils.clamp((r * r - lo * lo) / Math.max(1e-4, hi * hi - lo * lo), 0, 1);
```

WHY: the comment's premise is wrong — the void does not spawn at 1.0. `resetMatch` sets it to `START_R`:

```
6169:  curStage = 0; voidling.setStage(0); voidling.setRadius(START_R);
```

and `START_R = 0.9` (:3030). So the hard-coded `1` puts the bottom of the first rung *above* the spawn size, and `(0.81 - 1)` clamps to 0 for every radius from 0.9 to 1.0 — the first 12 % of the first rung's area is a dead band where eating moves nothing. The growth law reaches 1.0 at about 2.1 s (`lawCap = 0.9 + 0.047·el`), most of which the 2.2 s intro damp covers, so the visible cost is small; but the magic number is not the value the reasoning intended.

FIX: `const lo = Math.max(FORM_MIN[st], START_R)`.

GATE: `qa/_firstevolve.mjs` (or a two-line addition to `qa/smoke.mjs`): assert `formProgress` is 0 at spawn **and** strictly increasing on the first swallowed prop.

## One correction to the standing briefs

`docs/HANDOFF.md` trap #8 and `qa/README.md`'s "Async props" trap both say **"`glb()` registers props asynchronously … anything fingerprinting `__edibles` early counts a different world every run."** That is no longer true. `assets3d.ts:98` has no promise, no `.then`, no fetch — `if (!opts.fallback) return; const fb = opts.fallback(); … scene.add(fb); addEdible?.(fb, r);` — and `requestedReady()` (`assets3d.ts:36-46`) returns `Promise.resolve()` after reporting `1, 1`. `createIsland` is fully awaited before `initialMass = edibles.length` at `prototype3d.ts:9214`. The world is complete and identical the moment the boot cover drops.

Two live consequences: `_revalQueue = [tClock + 8, tClock + 22]` (`prototype3d.ts:5131`) re-sweeps twice mid-match for GLB arrivals that can no longer happen, and `validateWorld`'s "a GLB wrapper whose model hasn't streamed yet measures ~empty" guard (:5866) is dead code. Probes that "wait for a stable count" are waiting on nothing.

## Areas I looked at and found nothing real

- **`growRadius` boundaries.** `min(R_CAP, sqrt(R² + 0.5·eR²·rookie·diminish))` cannot produce a negative radicand (all terms non-negative), `diminish = sqrt(START_R / max(START_R, R))` is guarded against R=0, and `R_CAP` is 18 now, not the 12 in the brief — `LAW_TOP = 12` at :8194 is what binds ordinary play. No NaN reachable.
- **`FORM_MIN` / `formProgress` indexing.** `stageFor` caps at 6; `FORM_MIN[7] ?? R_CAP` handles the top rung; `FORM_MIN[Math.max(0, st-1)] || START_R` correctly rescues the falsy `FORM_MIN[0] === 0`.
- **`matchdeck.ts`.** `PAIRS[n % 4]` and `n % hours` are in range for every n; `MID_POOL` holds the *original* beat objects and `dealMids` assigns clones into the `BEATS` slots, so the jitter block at :5151 can never mutate a pool entry. The `bt.base` latch is correct across matches.
- **Empty catches / unhandled rejections.** Every `catch` in `prototype3d.ts` has a body or a documented fall-through; `preloadP` (`:5229`) can only resolve, so the two bare `Promise.race(...).then(...)` chains at :5330 and :5719 cannot reject.
- **Divide-by-zero.** `life.ts:415` guards `len > 1e-6`, `life.ts:4109` uses `|| 1`. The `dx/d` normalisations at `prototype3d.ts:4780` and `:8742` are measure-zero (they require a prop's centre to coincide exactly with the void's).
- **World switch.** It is a genuine `location.href = location.pathname` full reload at `:4689`, `:5590` and `:5615` — the whole document is replaced, so there is nothing to tear down.
- **Per-match listener accumulation.** All 64 `addEventListener` calls are module-scope or on nodes rebuilt by `innerHTML`; the drop orb uses `on*` property assignment, not `addEventListener`. `paused` is cleared on both exits from the pause sheet (`doQuit` calls `resume()` first at :6268).
- **Telemetry / kids privacy.** `analytics.ts` is opt-in default-off behind the parental gate, mints no persistent id, and actively deletes `vd_uid` and `vd_first_open` on load. Nothing leaves the device before consent.

COVERAGE: `docs/HANDOFF.md`, `docs/AAA-BRIEF.md` (§0–§4.1, §7 ledger incl. the WAIVED block and the last three owner rounds), `qa/README.md`, `src/prototype3d.ts` (lines 83–230, 295–320, 360–460, 760–850, 1690–1790, 2326–2400, 2496–2600, 2740–2830, 3010–3110, 3196–3500, 3560–3620, 3860–3930, 4040–4110, 4250–4360, 4377–4500, 4494–4760, 4770–4800, 4850–4950, 5040–5220, 5290–5360, 5560–5680, 5760–6020, 6020–6100, 6098–6320, 6380–6450, 7180–7215, 7810–7840, 7960–8100, 8130–8250, 8590–8760, 8925–8995, 9195–9228), `src/proto3d/rivals.ts` (1–60, 372–500, 640–700, 1290–1330), `src/proto3d/life.ts` (405–425, 2061, 4098–4120, 4260–4310), `src/proto3d/assets3d.ts` (36–170), `src/proto3d/void3d.ts` (1443–1480, 1720–1760), `src/game/matchdeck.ts` (whole), `src/game/analytics.ts` (whole), `src/proto3d/telemetry.ts` (1–80), `index.html` (1818–1829), `qa/_rf_evorefire.mjs`, `qa/_rf_evorefire2.mjs`, `docs/FABLE-BRIEF.md` (160–180, 280–300).
